Admission-race handling is #1485 and blocked-backlog scheduling is #1490.\n\n---\n## Historical requirements and evidence (preserved)\n\n> The current execution plan and acceptance additions above supersede conflicting historical implementation prescriptions and dependency lists below. The historical material records earlier findings; revalidate old claims against current source rather than treating them as new unfixed defects.\n\n\n## Problem\n\nformal-ai is a big Rust project with a JavaScript and TypeScript implementation. Rust CI/CD starts on every push without waiting for JavaScript checks. The JavaScript gate only parses files. PR #1188 shows the cost: many pushes, almost no green runs. This issue applies the rules from link-assistant/router#759 to this repository.\n\n## Findings\n\n1. **Rust jobs are not gated on JavaScript jobs.** In `.github/workflows/release.yml` the Rust jobs `lint` (line 279), `test` (357, matrix with `cargo test`) and `build` (592) depend only on `detect-changes` and `base`. `coverage.yml` and `layered-ci.yml` also trigger on their own on `pull_request`. No workflow uses `workflow_run`. `layered-ci.yml` orders js, ts and rust tiers only inside itself, and `release.yml` never waits for it.\n2. **The JavaScript gate checks syntax only.** The `js` job in `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml` (lines 89-118) runs `node --check`. The JavaScript tests (`npm run test:web`, `rust/tests/web/*.test.mjs`) run only in `coverage.yml:305` (as coverage) and `links.yml:63`. Both are outside any gate for Rust jobs.\n3. **No JS/Rust behaviour parity gate.** The `ts` tier checks that every `.js` file has a `.ts` sibling (file-set parity). No workflow checks a feature manifest or shared golden fixtures between the JavaScript and Rust implementations. `grep parity .github/workflows` finds only `layered-ci.yml`. CONTRIBUTING.md says the \"closed js-first loop\" is not claimed yet.\n4. **Skipped or cancelled upstream tiers let the next tier run.** `layered-ci.yml` lines 124 and 157 accept `needs.js.result == 'skipped'` and `needs.ts.result == 'skipped'` as pass. A path-filtered or cancelled JavaScript stage therefore does not block the Rust tier.\n5. **Runs are cancelled by the next push.** `release.yml`, `coverage.yml`, `layered-ci.yml` and others set `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, so every PR push cancels the Rust jobs. On #1188 (100 commits, +1,410,501/-200,572): `CI/CD Pipeline` 0/11 green (10 failed, 1 cancelled), `Layered CI` 0/12 (10 failed, 2 cancelled), `Coverage` 0/11 (6 failed, 5 cancelled), `Question necessity ratchet` 5/12 green (7 failed).\n6. **No required status checks on `main`.** The only ruleset, `protection`, has the rules `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`. It has no `required_status_checks` and no pull request rule (`gh api repos/link-assistant/formal-ai/rulesets`).\n7. **No documented single push gate for agents.** CONTRIBUTING.md has \"Work in bulk; verify selectively\" (~line 510) and \"push only after re-reading the issue\" but does not name one agent as the only pusher. It does not say to collect all failures of the latest run before one push, or to never push while a run is in progress. There is no `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` in the repository root.\n8. **Runner OS is not pinned.** `ubuntu-latest` appears 64 times in 28 workflow files. The shared Rust template uses `ubuntu-24.04` and hive-mind `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md` requires an explicit label.\n9. **Daily scheduled workflow is red.** `Self-development status` failed on `main` on 2026-10-05, 06, 07, 08 and 09 (`gh run list --branch main`). `External Benchmarks` also failed on 2026-10-05.\n10. **Stale open pull requests.** #887 (opened 2026-08-01), #652 (2026-07-12), #646 (2026-07-10), #644 and #643 (2026-07-08) are still open.\n11. **No measurement.** No document reports pushes per PR, runs per PR (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, or time to first fully green run for #1188 or a typical PR.\n\n## Requirements\n\n1. Make every Rust job (`lint`, `test`, `build`, coverage, e2e that compile Rust) depend on one JavaScript stage for the same commit. Use `needs:` in one workflow, or `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` and the same `head_sha` and no own `push`/`pull_request` trigger. Test: a PR with a failing JavaScript test starts zero Rust jobs.\n2. Extend the JavaScript stage to run lint, `npm run test:web`, `js/` and `ts/` tests, the js to ts regenerate-and-diff check and the parity check. It must run on every PR, including Rust-only changes.\n3. Add a parity manifest (for example `parity/features.json`, feature to JavaScript implementation, Rust implementation, evidence) with shared golden fixtures that both implementations must pass. Add a checker run in CI. Follow link-foundation/meta-language `parity/language-features.json` and `scripts/check-js-rust-parity.mjs`.\n4. Treat `skipped` and `cancelled` upstream results as failure for the Rust gate. Remove `|| skipped` acceptance in `layered-ci.yml` for the Rust tier, or replace it with an explicit \"unchanged, last green on same tree hash\" check.\n5. Set `cancel-in-progress: false` for the Rust stage on pull request branches, with one concurrency group per branch.\n6. Add a CI check script that fails if any workflow can start a Rust job without the JavaScript gate. Run it in `workflows.yml`.\n7. Add required status checks (the JavaScript stage, the Rust stage and `Pipeline Status`) to the `main` ruleset.\n8. Add the single push gate rules to CONTRIBUTING.md and a new `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`: drafting sub-agents never push; one CI/CD sub-agent pushes once, after collecting all failures of the latest run; never push while a run is in progress on the branch; run JavaScript checks locally before the push; no full local Rust builds unless the change is Rust-only. Include a bounded shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, limited `-j`, and pruning of old artifacts.\n9. Replace `ubuntu-latest` with `ubuntu-24.04` in all workflows and add a check in `scripts/check-ci-workflows`-style form (as in the JS template) that rejects `-latest` labels.\n10. Fix or disable `Self-development status` so it is green on `main` for 7 days. Record the root cause in the case study.\n11. Merge or close #887, #652, #646, #644, #643, or comment why each stays open. Add a stale-PR report to the weekly status job.\n12. Write `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` with before/after numbers for #1188: pushes, CI runs (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, time to first fully green run, peak local RSS and disk of an agent task. Acceptance: the next large PR shows at most one full Rust run per push group and a green first Rust run after the JavaScript stage is green.\n\n## Related\n\n- link-assistant/router#759 (the standard this issue applies)\n- link-assistant/formal-ai#1138 (js to ts to rust cycle, source of `layered-ci.yml`); partly covers findings 1 to 4\n- link-assistant/formal-ai#1187 (credentials in workflows; touches `Layered CI` dispatch only, not covering gating)\n- link-assistant/formal-ai#1168 and #1169 (pin latest action and dependency versions; does not cover runner OS labels)\n- link-assistant/formal-ai#1084 (multi-arch images, CI-CD best practice 13)\n- link-assistant/hive-mind `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`\n- link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template and link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template\n\n---\nWe need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).\n\nIf there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.\n\nIf issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Pull requests compile no Rust and build no Docker image here, so the production after-numbers come from the first default-branch runs (see *Pending*).\n\nDesign notes, objectives and tradeoffs: [`docs/ci-cd/speed.md` → Hive feedback loop (issue #1486)](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/issue-1486-ec1670239452/docs/ci-cd/speed.md#hive-feedback-loop-issue-1486)\n\n## Baseline (before), measured per phase\n\nMeasured by `scripts/ci-phase-timing.mjs` from the recorded API data (fixtures in `data/benchmarks/ci-phase-timing/baseline-runs/`):\n\n| Run | Wall | Main phases | Attempts |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Draft [41191429608](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/41191429608) | 1337 s | queue 87 s, checkout 305 s, cold compile 353 s, image prep 106 s, solver 414 s | 0/1 useful |\n| Delivery [40475832633](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/40475832633) | 4734 s | image prep 952 s; image download per leg 1882 / 1187 / 571 s; image load per leg up to 407 s; binary extraction 373 s; solver 1140 s total | 3/3 useful |\n\nThe delivery candidate archive was 8.48 GB per leg. The base `konard/hive-mind-dind` is 87 layers and 9.43 GB compressed (amd64 registry manifest), so nearly all of that transfer was base layers.\n\n## Changes per step of the issue\n\n1. **Phase instrumentation.**\n   - `scripts/lib/ci-phase-timing.mjs` and `scripts/ci-phase-timing.mjs` split a run into queue, runner, checkout, install, compile, image prep, image transfer, image load, solver, verification and publication.\n   - They record artifact, image-bundle and image-transfer bytes, and total, useful and skipped solver attempts.\n   - A skipped step adds no time and no attempt. An expired artifact counts as unknown, not as 0 bytes.\n   - `.github/workflows/ci-phase-timing.yml` (read-only token) measures every executed default-branch draft or delivery completion, and runs a daily check.\n2. **Replay tests and focused-test map.**\n   - `scripts/extract-draft-replay.mjs` turns a draft session artifact into a fixture.\n   - `rust/tests/web/draft-request-replay.test.mjs` replays the captured run 41191429608 (`ReadPolicyRefused`) with no Docker, release or Rust build.\n   - `data/benchmarks/focused-test-map.json` with `scripts/select-focused-tests.mjs` maps components and failure reasons to tests.\n   - Layered CI shard 1 runs the mapped tests for the changed files first.\n3. **One build per identity.**\n   - `scripts/lib/formal-ai-build-identity.mjs` and `scripts/formal-ai-shared-build.mjs` define the identity: source tree, `rustc -vV`, target, profile, features, binary, `Cargo.lock` digest and build recipe.\n   - The earliest live claim produces the build. Other drafts wait up to 600 s for its product, then verify producer workflow, branch, event, repository, identity, SHA-256 and size before using it.\n   - A failed build publishes nothing. A stale, poisoned, incomplete or mismatched product is rejected and the draft builds for itself.\n   - `hive-mind-draft.yml` records `build_mode` and `FORMAL_AI_BINARY_SOURCE`.\n4. **Separate base layers.**\n   - `scripts/lib/oci-delta-archive.mjs` and bundle schema `formal-ai-hive-image-bundle/v2` ship only the layers the candidate adds over its digest-pinned base.\n   - Each leg pulls the base by digest, checks its image ID and diffIDs, loads the delta, and still requires the exact producer image ID. A cached image is never substituted.\n   - When the delta cannot be proven, the full archive ships with the reason recorded.\n5. **Sequential or parallel clients:** keep parallel. Per leg, setup before the solver is about 25 min and the solve 364–407 s. Running the three sequentially would exceed the 30-minute job limit and would share one Docker daemon between clients that are judged independently. The delta removes the duplicated cost instead.\n6. **Full qualification stays at its boundary.** Oracles, native qualification, independent verification, effect claims and publication are unchanged.\n7. **Numeric objectives and alerts.**\n   - `data/benchmarks/ci-phase-timing/slo.json` sets limits: draft queue 300 s, warm compile 60 s, cold compile 720 s, draft wall 1800 s, delivery image prep 1200 s, image transfer per leg 300 s, load per leg 600 s, image bundle 2 GiB, delivery wall 3600 s.\n   - A breach in all of the latest 3 applicable runs fails the job with `::error`. A single breach is a warning.\n   - The delivery workflow excludes \"Hive CI phase timing\" from its `workflow_run` trigger, so measuring it does not admit another delivery run.\n\n## How to reproduce\n\n```bash\n# Captured planner failure, offline: fails on the captured source edf219e6 (ReadPolicyRefused), passes here\nbash experiments/issue-1486/replay-on-captured-source.sh\nnode --test rust/tests/web/draft-request-replay.test.mjs\n\n# Delta image transport on a small base (needs Docker; not run in PR CI)\nbash experiments/issue-1486/delta-image-probe.sh\n\n# Phase timing and objectives on the recorded baseline runs\nnode scripts/ci-phase-timing.mjs check --fixtures data/benchmarks/ci-phase-timing/baseline-runs\nnode scripts/ci-phase-timing.mjs measure --run <run-id>   # any live run, needs GH_TOKEN\n\n# Focused tests for a change\nnode scripts/select-focused-tests.mjs --base origin/main --run\n```\n\nOffline check output: delivery 40475832633 breaches `delivery-image-transfer-per-leg` (1882 s > 300 s) and `delivery-wall` (4734 s > 3600 s). Every other baseline is within its limit.\n\nDelta probe (local Docker, small base): the full archive was 3,976,226 B and the delta 203,335 B. The delta loads to the exact candidate ID when the base is present. Keep the single Formal AI CI\nbuild and select the matching versioned Hive Mind image without a stale-image\nfallback. Log versions and hashes; retain failure evidence and respond to the\nissue even when initial source discovery fails. CLI integration uses the latest\npublished Hive Mind package. Frozen historical replays remain explicitly\nhistorical, not current-runtime qualification.\n\nNative release import materializes its authenticated offline worktree once.\nVerify the commit, tree, lock bytes and native-input bytes after restoration;\ndo not repeat a full checkout-index rewrite. Keep complete unfiltered history,\nuse at most four checkout workers, bound each history command to four minutes\nand the restore transaction to six, and give the workflow import step a\nseven-minute backstop. Tests trace actual Git operations against small offline\nfixtures; all Rust compilation and package execution remain in CI.\n\nDecorative live badge outages must not block coding and release delivery. Keep\nexceptions anchored to the exact image URL with the observed CI evidence; keep\nchecking its artifact destination and other URLs. A badge exception grants no\npublication evidence and must not accept HTTP 408 globally or expand retry limits.\nThe link workflow runs the small real-HTTP timeout and missing-page regressions.\n\nKeep main stable throughout production publication, not just version preparation.\nThe release checks freshness again after compilation. Continue drafting fixes\nwhile CI runs, but hold routine merges until publication and the release consumers\nare verified. If a critical fix must supersede a failed release, let the fresh\nmain run deliver it; do not weaken source checks or retry the superseded run.\nSee [the release handoff guide](release-handoff.md).\n\nDocumentation-only automatic changes use the policy in\n[`scripts/documentation-only-ci-policy.mjs`](../../scripts/documentation-only-ci-policy.mjs): skip\nheavy workflows and automatic releases, retain lightweight checks and explicit\nmanual controls. The bot dispatch action observes the same policy. A pending\nchangelog fragment cannot override it. Mixed source changes and unknown runtime\nMarkdown retain normal CI; GitHub's large-diff limits can reduce filtering savings.\nSee [the requirements](../requirements/issue-1455-documentation-and-evidence.md).\nThe separate provenance performance qualification and real Agent CLI\nfailure-report replay are retained as main-only manual qualifications; their native\ncompilation does not run in the default PR profile. Default deferral is recorded\nexplicitly and provides no execution credit. Production compilation and native\ntests still run on main.\n\n- **No job or step runs longer than 30 minutes.** 15 minutes is the target.\n  Every job declares `timeout-minutes` at or under 30, and so does every step\n  in it. No job's measured maximum is above 30 minutes either.\n- **Long work starts first.** Small jobs fill the capacity left once the long\n  jobs are running. This holds at two levels:\n  - **Jobs on parallel machines.** A long job (measured median of 10 minutes\n    or more) has `needs:` only on jobs whose outputs, results or artifacts it\n    uses. It never waits on a fast lint job it does not depend on.\n  - **Tests inside a job.** Sharded suites are split longest-first from\n    recorded durations, never dealt out by listed index. The files of a\n    JavaScript shard run on every core, longest first.\n- **Sharding loses nothing.** The plan puts every listed test in exactly one\n  shard. Each shard re-checks this on the real listing before it runs its\n  part.\n\n## How it is enforced\n\n`node scripts/check-ci-speed.mjs` is the gate. It is registered in\n[`data/meta/ci-gates/check-ci-speed.lino`](../../data/meta/ci-gates/check-ci-speed.lino)\nand runs in the `lint` job, and `--report` also prints each workflow's\ncritical path. The rule and its exceptions live in\n[`data/meta/ci-speed.lino`](../../data/meta/ci-speed.lino). The gate fails when:\n\n- a job has no `timeout-minutes`, or a job or step cap is above the limit,\n  and no `over-limit-job` entry allows it;\n- a job's measured maximum in\n  [`data/meta/ci-durations.lino`](../../data/meta/ci-durations.lino) is above\n  the limit, and no entry covers it;\n- an `over-limit-job` entry no longer excuses anything, because the job now\n  meets the limit or is gone. The exception list only shrinks;\n- a long job `needs:` a job whose outputs, results or artifacts it does not\n  use;\n- a workflow or `scripts/*.sh` file shards tests by index\n  (`(NR - 1) % n`, `position % SHARD_TOTAL`, `--test-shard`,\n  `--partition slice:`);\n- a `sharded-suite` does not plan its shards with\n  `scripts/plan-test-shards.mjs`;\n- the planner loses, repeats or misorders a recorded test for any shard\n  count from 1 to 12.\n\n`rust/tests/web/ci-speed.test.mjs` pins each of these on small inputs, and\nthen on the real tree.\n\n## Test shards, longest first\n\n`scripts/plan-test-shards.mjs` reads a test listing on stdin, one test per\nline, optionally as `<executable>\\t<test>`. It prints one shard's part:\n\n```sh\ndist/tests/unit --list --format terse | sed -n 's/: test$//p' \\\n  | node scripts/plan-test-shards.mjs --shard 2 --of 4\n```\n\nThe planner works like this:\n\n- It sorts the tests longest first.\n- It gives each test to the shard with the least work so far. This is the\n  longest-processing-time rule; Graham's bound keeps the slowest shard within\n  4/3 of the optimum.\n- Ties break by name, so every shard computes the same plan on its own.\n- `--reserve \"1=330,2=80\"` tells it that a shard already carries other work,\n  such as the full lane's data-integrity and census gates on shard 1, so that\n  shard gets fewer tests.\n- `--check` exits non-zero unless the shards cover the listing exactly once.\n- `--report` prints each shard's predicted seconds.\n\nThe planner is used by:\n\n- the full Rust lane (`scripts/run-prebuilt-tests.sh`, four shards over the\n  unit, integration and source executables together);\n- the specification lane (the `Run specification tests from the prebuilt\n  binary` step in `release.yml`);\n- the coverage shards (`scripts/run-coverage-shard.sh`);\n- the Layered CI js tier, which plans the files under `rust/tests/web/` and\n  runs them with `node --test --test-concurrency=\"$(nproc)\"`.\n\nA test with no recorded duration counts as `default-seconds` (0.1 s unless\nthe file sets it). A new test still runs exactly once, and its weight only\naffects balance.\n\n## Refreshing the durations\n\nEvery record is generated, never edited by hand. The generator only reads\nfrom GitHub with `gh`:\n\n| Record | Command | Source |\n|---|---|---|\n| `data/meta/ci-durations.lino` | `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/ci-durations.mjs --write [--branch B] [--runs N]` | The last N completed, non-cancelled runs of every workflow on the branch. It records each job's median and maximum minutes, and the run wall-clock. |\n| `data/meta/test-durations.lino` | `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/ci-durations.mjs --tests --write [--run ID]` | The `Test (…)` job logs of a CI/CD Pipeline run with per-test times. |\n| `data/meta/javascript-test-durations.lino` | `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/ci-durations.mjs --javascript-files --write` | Each suite file run alone on the local machine. Only the order carries over to CI. |\n\nPer-test Rust times come from libtest's `--report-time`. On a stable\ntoolchain that flag needs `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP`, which reaches every process the\ntests spawn, so it is off by default. To record the times for one run:\n\n1. Set the repository variable `FORMAL_AI_RECORD_TEST_TIMES` to `true`.\n2. Push, or re-run the CI/CD Pipeline.\n3. Run `--tests --write` against that run.\n4. Unset the variable.\n\n## What is still over the limit\n\nThe `over-limit-job` entries in `data/meta/ci-speed.lino` are the current\ndebt. Log versions and hashes; retain failure evidence and respond to the\nissue even when initial source discovery fails. CLI integration uses the latest\npublished Hive Mind package. Frozen historical replays remain explicitly\nhistorical, not current-runtime qualification.\n\nNative release import materializes its authenticated offline worktree once.\nVerify the commit, tree, lock bytes and native-input bytes after restoration;\ndo not repeat a full checkout-index rewrite. Keep complete unfiltered history,\nuse at most four checkout workers, bound each history command to four minutes\nand the restore transaction to six, and give the workflow import step a\nseven-minute backstop. Tests trace actual Git operations against small offline\nfixtures; all Rust compilation and package execution remain in CI.\n\nDecorative live badge outages must not block coding and release delivery. Keep\nexceptions anchored to the exact image URL with the observed CI evidence; keep\nchecking its artifact destination and other URLs. A badge exception grants no\npublication evidence and must not accept HTTP 408 globally or expand retry limits.\nThe link workflow runs the small real-HTTP timeout and missing-page regressions.\n\nKeep main stable throughout production publication, not just version preparation.\nThe release checks freshness again after compilation. Continue drafting fixes\nwhile CI runs, but hold routine merges until publication and the release consumers\nare verified. If a critical fix must supersede a failed release, let the fresh\nmain run deliver it; do not weaken source checks or retry the superseded run.\nSee [the release handoff guide](release-handoff.md).\n\nDocumentation-only automatic changes use the policy in\n[`scripts/documentation-only-ci-policy.mjs`](../../scripts/documentation-only-ci-policy.mjs): skip\nheavy workflows and automatic releases, retain lightweight checks and explicit\nmanual controls. The bot dispatch action observes the same policy. A pending\nchangelog fragment cannot override it. Mixed source changes and unknown runtime\nMarkdown retain normal CI; GitHub's large-diff limits can reduce filtering savings.\nSee [the requirements](../requirements/issue-1455-documentation-and-evidence.md).\nThe separate provenance performance qualification and real Agent CLI\nfailure-report replay are retained as main-only manual qualifications; their native\ncompilation does not run in the default PR profile. Default deferral is recorded\nexplicitly and provides no execution credit. Production compilation and native\ntests still run on main.\n\n- **No job or step runs longer than 30 minutes.** 15 minutes is the target.\n  Every job declares `timeout-minutes` at or under 30, and so does every step\n  in it. No job's measured maximum is above 30 minutes either.\n- **Long work starts first.** Small jobs fill the capacity left once the long\n  jobs are running. This holds at two levels:\n  - **Jobs on parallel machines.** A long job (measured median of 10 minutes\n    or more) has `needs:` only on jobs whose outputs, results or artifacts it\n    uses. It never waits on a fast lint job it does not depend on.\n  - **Tests inside a job.** Sharded suites are split longest-first from\n    recorded durations, never dealt out by listed index. The files of a\n    JavaScript shard run on every core, longest first.\n- **Sharding loses nothing.** The plan puts every listed test in exactly one\n  shard. Each shard re-checks this on the real listing before it runs its\n  part.\n\n## How it is enforced\n\n`node scripts/check-ci-speed.mjs` is the gate. It is registered in\n[`data/meta/ci-gates/check-ci-speed.lino`](../../data/meta/ci-gates/check-ci-speed.lino)\nand runs in the `lint` job, and `--report` also prints each workflow's\ncritical path. The rule and its exceptions live in\n[`data/meta/ci-speed.lino`](../../data/meta/ci-speed.lino). The gate fails when:\n\n- a job has no `timeout-minutes`, or a job or step cap is above the limit,\n  and no `over-limit-job` entry allows it;\n- a job's measured maximum in\n  [`data/meta/ci-durations.lino`](../../data/meta/ci-durations.lino) is above\n  the limit, and no entry covers it;\n- an `over-limit-job` entry no longer excuses anything, because the job now\n  meets the limit or is gone. The exception list only shrinks;\n- a long job `needs:` a job whose outputs, results or artifacts it does not\n  use;\n- a workflow or `scripts/*.sh` file shards tests by index\n  (`(NR - 1) % n`, `position % SHARD_TOTAL`, `--test-shard`,\n  `--partition slice:`);\n- a `sharded-suite` does not plan its shards with\n  `scripts/plan-test-shards.mjs`;\n- the planner loses, repeats or misorders a recorded test for any shard\n  count from 1 to 12.\n\n`rust/tests/web/ci-speed.test.mjs` pins each of these on small inputs, and\nthen on the real tree.\n\n## Test shards, longest first\n\n`scripts/plan-test-shards.mjs` reads a test listing on stdin, one test per\nline, optionally as `<executable>\\t<test>`. It prints one shard's part:\n\n```sh\ndist/tests/unit --list --format terse | sed -n 's/: test$//p' \\\n  | node scripts/plan-test-shards.mjs --shard 2 --of 4\n```\n\nThe planner works like this:\n\n- It sorts the tests longest first.\n- It gives each test to the shard with the least work so far. This is the\n  longest-processing-time rule; Graham's bound keeps the slowest shard within\n  4/3 of the optimum.\n- Ties break by name, so every shard computes the same plan on its own.\n- `--reserve \"1=330,2=80\"` tells it that a shard already carries other work,\n  such as the full lane's data-integrity and census gates on shard 1, so that\n  shard gets fewer tests.\n- `--check` exits non-zero unless the shards cover the listing exactly once.\n- `--report` prints each shard's predicted seconds.\n\nThe planner is used by:\n\n- the full Rust lane (`scripts/run-prebuilt-tests.sh`, four shards over the\n  unit, integration and source executables together);\n- the specification lane (the `Run specification tests from the prebuilt\n  binary` step in `release.yml`);\n- the coverage shards (`scripts/run-coverage-shard.sh`);\n- the Layered CI js tier, which plans the files under `rust/tests/web/` and\n  runs them with `node --test --test-concurrency=\"$(nproc)\"`.\n\nA test with no recorded duration counts as `default-seconds` (0.1 s unless\nthe file sets it). A new test still runs exactly once, and its weight only\naffects balance.\n\n## Refreshing the durations\n\nEvery record is generated, never edited by hand. The generator only reads\nfrom GitHub with `gh`:\n\n| Record | Command | Source |\n|---|---|---|\n| `data/meta/ci-durations.lino` | `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/ci-durations.mjs --write [--branch B] [--runs N]` | The last N completed, non-cancelled runs of every workflow on the branch. It records each job's median and maximum minutes, and the run wall-clock. |\n| `data/meta/test-durations.lino` | `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/ci-durations.mjs --tests --write [--run ID]` | The `Test (…)` job logs of a CI/CD Pipeline run with per-test times. |\n| `data/meta/javascript-test-durations.lino` | `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/ci-durations.mjs --javascript-files --write` | Each suite file run alone on the local machine. Only the order carries over to CI. |\n\nPer-test Rust times come from libtest's `--report-time`. On a stable\ntoolchain that flag needs `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP`, which reaches every process the\ntests spawn, so it is off by default. To record the times for one run:\n\n1. Set the repository variable `FORMAL_AI_RECORD_TEST_TIMES` to `true`.\n2. Push, or re-run the CI/CD Pipeline.\n3. Run `--tests --write` against that run.\n4. Unset the variable.\n\n## What is still over the limit\n\nThe `over-limit-job` entries in `data/meta/ci-speed.lino` are the current\ndebt. Each entry gives its measured numbers, the reason it is still over the\nlimit, and what would bring it under. Most of them never run on a pull\nrequest: release publishing, Pages deployment, scheduled refreshes, and\nmacOS while non-Linux CI is off. The ones that do run on pull requests are:\n\n- the release `test` cap (measured at most 19.3 minutes, but sized by the\n  issue #1081 budget-share rule);\n- the coverage build;\n- the local web-app E2E suite (30.0 minutes at most);\n- the agent CLI E2E legs;\n- the desktop packaging builds;\n- the agent ladder's static 180-minute cap, which the wall-clock record\n  [`data/meta/ci-wall-clock.lino`](../../data/meta/ci-wall-clock.lino) reads.\n\n## Temporary critical coding profile (2026-10-27)\n\nThe current priority is a usable Linux/Docker release that can solve small\ncoding tasks, answer questions, report failures and retain evidence for learning.\nThe 2026-10-28 fast PR policy supersedes the earlier all-integrations-on-PR\nprofile: Linux JavaScript/TypeScript behavior and consistency checks remain on\nPRs; native production compilation/tests, package and image builds, native parity,\nsource-network serialization, native measurement and broad benchmark/client integration jobs are\nretained for main; complete Coding Ladder measurement requires explicit opt-in. Measured from the recorded runs (kept as\nreplayable API fixtures in\n[`data/benchmarks/ci-phase-timing/baseline-runs/`](../../data/benchmarks/ci-phase-timing/baseline-runs/)):\n\n| Run | Phase | Before |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Draft 41191429608 | queue / checkout / compile / solver | 87 s / 305 s / 353 s cold Cargo build / 414 s (failed) |\n| Delivery 40475832633 | image preparation (build 887 s + free disk 65 s) | 952 s |\n| Delivery 40475832633 | image download per leg (codex / agent / claude) | 1882 s / 1187 s / 571 s |\n| Delivery 40475832633 | image load per leg | 310 s / 406 s / 369 s |\n| Delivery 40475832633 | candidate archive per leg | 8.48 GB, three times |\n| Delivery 40475832633 | wall time | 4734 s for 3 useful attempts |\n\n### Phases, bytes and objectives\n\n`scripts/ci-phase-timing.mjs` splits a completed run into queue, runner,\ncheckout, install, compile, image preparation, image transfer, image load,\nsolver, verification and publication from the Actions API. It also records\nartifact, image-bundle and image-transfer bytes and the total, useful and\nskipped solver attempts. A skipped step adds no seconds and no attempt. An\nexpired artifact is reported as unknown, never as zero bytes.\n\n`.github/workflows/ci-phase-timing.yml` runs on every executed default-branch\ndraft or delivery completion, while the one-day image artifact still exists,\nand once a day. It writes the per-phase table to the step summary and keeps the\nJSON for 90 days. The objectives in\n[`slo.json`](../../data/benchmarks/ci-phase-timing/slo.json) apply per run that\nexecuted a solver:\n\n| Objective | Limit | Baseline |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| draft queue | 300 s | 87 s |\n| draft compile, warm (shared build reused) | 60 s | none: every draft compiled |\n| draft compile, cold | 720 s | 353 s |\n| draft wall | 1800 s | 1337 s |\n| delivery image preparation | 1200 s | 952 s |\n| delivery image transfer, per leg | 300 s | 1882 s |\n| delivery image load and base pull, per leg | 600 s | 407 s |\n| delivery image bundle | 2 GiB (every run) | 8.48 GB |\n| delivery wall | 3600 s | 4734 s |\n\nA breach in every one of the latest three applicable runs fails the job with an\n`::error`; that red run is the alert. A single breach is a warning. Measure a\nrun or replay the baselines offline with:\n\n    node scripts/ci-phase-timing.mjs measure --run <id>\n    node scripts/ci-phase-timing.mjs check --fixtures data/benchmarks/ci-phase-timing/baseline-runs\n\n### Focused offline checks first\n\n[`focused-test-map.json`](../../data/benchmarks/focused-test-map.json) maps\ncomponents and captured failure reasons to their offline tests.\n`node scripts/select-focused-tests.mjs --base origin/main --run` runs only the\nmapped tests, one at a time. `scripts/extract-draft-replay.mjs` turns a\ndownloaded draft session artifact into a fixture under\n`data/benchmarks/fixtures/draft-replays/`, and `draft-request-replay.test.mjs`\nreplays it with no Docker, release or Rust compilation. The captured run\n41191429608 (`ReadPolicyRefused`) fails on its source and passes on the fix;\n`experiments/issue-1486/replay-on-captured-source.sh` reproduces both.\n\n### One build per identity\n\nA draft computes its build identity from the source tree, `rustc -vV`, target,\nprofile, features, binary, `Cargo.lock` digest and the build recipe\n(`scripts/lib/formal-ai-build-identity.mjs`). The earliest live, authenticated\nclaim for that key builds; the others wait for its product (at most 600 s) and\nverify the producer workflow, branch, event and repository, the identity, and\nthe binary's SHA-256 and size before using it. A failed build publishes no\nproduct. A stale, poisoned, incomplete or mismatched product is rejected, and\nthe consumer builds for itself.\n\n### Image layers: transfer only what the candidate adds\n\nThe task image is built `FROM` the runtime image pinned by digest. The bundle\nnow carries a delta archive that omits the base layers the candidate inherits\nas an exact prefix (`scripts/lib/oci-delta-archive.mjs`, bundle schema\n`formal-ai-hive-image-bundle/v2`). Each leg pulls the base by digest, checks\nits image ID and layer diffIDs against the producer's identity, loads the\ndelta, and still requires the exact producer image ID. A missing or different\nbase fails the load. A cached image is never substituted for the candidate.\nWhen the delta cannot be proven (base not a prefix, base not pinned, the\ncontainerd store's blob names, or an incomplete stream), the full archive ships\nand the bundle records why.\n\n`experiments/issue-1486/delta-image-probe.sh` shows the mechanism locally on a\nsmall base: the full archive was 3,976,226 bytes and the delta 203,335 bytes.\nThe delta loaded to the exact candidate ID, and without its base the load\nfailed with the missing blob. The delivery base, `konard/hive-mind-dind`, is\n87 layers and 9.43 GB compressed (amd64 registry manifest), so nearly all of\nthe 8.48 GB per-leg transfer is base layers.\n\nCold and warm tradeoffs:\n\n- A fresh hosted runner has no layers, so each leg now pulls the base from the\n  registry instead of the Actions artifact store. The registry is usually\n  faster than the artifact store and the pull is digest-verified.\n- Registry rate limits and outages become a dependency of every leg. A failed\n  pull fails the leg closed; it never falls back to an unverified image.\n- A warm runner, or a later stage on the same runner, reuses the base layers\n  from the local store by content address.\n- The image job still builds the candidate once per run. The delta saves the\n  per-leg upload and download, not the build.\n\n### Sequential or parallel clients\n\nThe three clients stay parallel. A leg spends about 25 minutes before its\nsolver (image download 571–1882 s, load 310–406 s, plus checkout and claims)\nand 364–407 s solving. Run sequentially on one runner, setup plus three solves\nwould exceed the 30-minute job limit even with the delta transfer. It would\nalso share one Docker daemon and disk between clients that are now isolated\nand judged independently. The delta removes the duplicated cost instead.\n\n### What stays at its boundary\n\nFull oracles, native qualification, independent verification, the effect\nclaims and publication are unchanged. Pull requests still compile no Rust and\nbuild no Docker image, so the after-measurements come from the first\ndefault-branch draft and delivery runs measured by `ci-phase-timing.yml`.\nThe delivery job keeps its recorded 55-minute exception until those\nmeasurements show it fits under 30 minutes. Each draft keeps its own\n`hive-mind-draft-session-<issue>-<attempt>` artifact and outcome, and each\ndelivery leg keeps its own claim, result and evidence.\n# Essential PR checks and default-branch builds\n\nMaintainer requirements of 2026-10-31 supersede earlier full-PR build opt-ins.\n\n- PRs and checks dispatched on feature branches run essential Linux JavaScript\n  unit, coding, question-answering, reporting, policy and security checks. The closest results cover related issues.\n\n- **Kernel behavior:** A GNU bug thread shows that the kernel returns EEXIST when `mkdir` hits an existing path, whatever kind of file is there. A system call trace shows an lstat that returns ENOENT, followed by a mkdir that returns EEXIST. That sequence is the classic check-then-create gap.\n- **Check-then-create race:** In the same bug thread, one participant argues that the race condition is created when trying to stat(2) the file to see why it failed, because that check cannot be atomic with the creation.\n- **Parallel builds:** An Ubuntu bug about `install -D` in rust-coreutils describes a case where one thread successfully creates \"dir\"; when the remaining threads get mkdir(\"dir\")=EEXIST, the command exits with an error. So the losing callers fail rather than both succeeding.\n- **The uutils-specific issue:** CVE-2026-35353 covers a TOCTOU race in uutils `mkdir` when `-m` is used. The mkdir utility creates directories with default umask-derived permissions before applying the requested mode via chmod, which opens a brief window. The fix is in uutils 0.6.0 according to the coreutils 0.6.0 release tag and the linked pull request.\n\nFrom general knowledge rather than these results: `mkdir(2)` is atomic for a given path, so one call gets EEXIST and the other succeeds. Any \"both succeed\" symptom would more likely come from a non-atomic `-p` path or from the permission window above. Checking the uutils source and its issue tracker would be the next step.\n\n\nREMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks."

Rust CI/CD starts on every push without waiting for JavaScript checks. The JavaScript gate only parses files. PR #1188 shows the cost: many pushes, almost no green runs. This issue applies the rules from link-assistant/router#759 to this repository.\n\n## Findings\n\n1. **Rust jobs are not gated on JavaScript jobs.** In `.github/workflows/release.yml` the Rust jobs `lint` (line 279), `test` (357, matrix with `cargo test`) and `build` (592) depend only on `detect-changes` and `base`. `coverage.yml` and `layered-ci.yml` also trigger on their own on `pull_request`. No workflow uses `workflow_run`. `layered-ci.yml` orders js, ts and rust tiers only inside itself, and `release.yml` never waits for it.\n2. **The JavaScript gate checks syntax only.** The `js` job in `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml` (lines 89-118) runs `node --check`. The JavaScript tests (`npm run test:web`, `rust/tests/web/*.test.mjs`) run only in `coverage.yml:305` (as coverage) and `links.yml:63`. Both are outside any gate for Rust jobs.\n3. **No JS/Rust behaviour parity gate.** The `ts` tier checks that every `.js` file has a `.ts` sibling (file-set parity). No workflow checks a feature manifest or shared golden fixtures between the JavaScript and Rust implementations. `grep parity .github/workflows` finds only `layered-ci.yml`. CONTRIBUTING.md says the \"closed js-first loop\" is not claimed yet.\n4. **Skipped or cancelled upstream tiers let the next tier run.** `layered-ci.yml` lines 124 and 157 accept `needs.js.result == 'skipped'` and `needs.ts.result == 'skipped'` as pass. A path-filtered or cancelled JavaScript stage therefore does not block the Rust tier.\n5. **Runs are cancelled by the next push.** `release.yml`, `coverage.yml`, `layered-ci.yml` and others set `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, so every PR push cancels the Rust jobs. On #1188 (100 commits, +1,410,501/-200,572): `CI/CD Pipeline` 0/11 green (10 failed, 1 cancelled), `Layered CI` 0/12 (10 failed, 2 cancelled), `Coverage` 0/11 (6 failed, 5 cancelled), `Question necessity ratchet` 5/12 green (7 failed).\n6. **No required status checks on `main`.** The only ruleset, `protection`, has the rules `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`. It has no `required_status_checks` and no pull request rule (`gh api repos/link-assistant/formal-ai/rulesets`).\n7. **No documented single push gate for agents.** CONTRIBUTING.md has \"Work in bulk; verify selectively\" (~line 510) and \"push only after re-reading the issue\" but does not name one agent as the only pusher. It does not say to collect all failures of the latest run before one push, or to never push while a run is in progress. There is no `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` in the repository root.\n8. **Runner OS is not pinned.** `ubuntu-latest` appears 64 times in 28 workflow files. The shared Rust template uses `ubuntu-24.04` and hive-mind `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md` requires an explicit label.\n9. **Daily scheduled workflow is red.** `Self-development status` failed on `main` on 2026-10-05, 06, 07, 08 and 09 (`gh run list --branch main`). `External Benchmarks` also failed on 2026-10-05.\n10. **Stale open pull requests.** #887 (opened 2026-08-01), #652 (2026-07-12), #646 (2026-07-10), #644 and #643 (2026-07-08) are still open.\n11. **No measurement.** No document reports pushes per PR, runs per PR (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, or time to first fully green run for #1188 or a typical PR.\n\n## Requirements\n\n1. Make every Rust job (`lint`, `test`, `build`, coverage, e2e that compile Rust) depend on one JavaScript stage for the same commit. Use `needs:` in one workflow, or `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` and the same `head_sha` and no own `push`/`pull_request` trigger. Test: a PR with a failing JavaScript test starts zero Rust jobs.\n2. Extend the JavaScript stage to run lint, `npm run test:web`, `js/` and `ts/` tests, the js to ts regenerate-and-diff check and the parity check. It must run on every PR, including Rust-only changes.\n3. Add a parity manifest (for example `parity/features.json`, feature to JavaScript implementation, Rust implementation, evidence) with shared golden fixtures that both implementations must pass. Add a checker run in CI. Follow link-foundation/meta-language `parity/language-features.json` and `scripts/check-js-rust-parity.mjs`.\n4. Treat `skipped` and `cancelled` upstream results as failure for the Rust gate. Remove `|| skipped` acceptance in `layered-ci.yml` for the Rust tier, or replace it with an explicit \"unchanged, last green on same tree hash\" check.\n5. Set `cancel-in-progress: false` for the Rust stage on pull request branches, with one concurrency group per branch.\n6. Add a CI check script that fails if any workflow can start a Rust job without the JavaScript gate. Run it in `workflows.yml`.\n7. Add required status checks (the JavaScript stage, the Rust stage and `Pipeline Status`) to the `main` ruleset.\n8. Add the single push gate rules to CONTRIBUTING.md and a new `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`: drafting sub-agents never push; one CI/CD sub-agent pushes once, after collecting all failures of the latest run; never push while a run is in progress on the branch; run JavaScript checks locally before the push; no full local Rust builds unless the change is Rust-only. Include a bounded shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, limited `-j`, and pruning of old artifacts.\n9. Replace `ubuntu-latest` with `ubuntu-24.04` in all workflows and add a check in `scripts/check-ci-workflows`-style form (as in the JS template) that rejects `-latest` labels.\n10. Fix or disable `Self-development status` so it is green on `main` for 7 days. Record the root cause in the case study.\n11. Merge or close #887, #652, #646, #644, #643, or comment why each stays open. Add a stale-PR report to the weekly status job.\n12. Write `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` with before/after numbers for #1188: pushes, CI runs (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, time to first fully green run, peak local RSS and disk of an agent task. Acceptance: the next large PR shows at most one full Rust run per push group and a green first Rust run after the JavaScript stage is green.\n\n## Related\n\n- link-assistant/router#759 (the standard this issue applies)\n- link-assistant/formal-ai#1138 (js to ts to rust cycle, source of `layered-ci.yml`); partly covers findings 1 to 4\n- link-assistant/formal-ai#1187 (credentials in workflows; touches `Layered CI` dispatch only, not covering gating)\n- link-assistant/formal-ai#1168 and #1169 (pin latest action and dependency versions; does not cover runner OS labels)\n- link-assistant/formal-ai#1084 (multi-arch images, CI-CD best practice 13)\n- link-assistant/hive-mind `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`\n- link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template and link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template\n\n---\nWe need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).\n\nIf there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.\n\nIf issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. numbers. The proof below refutes the claim.\\n\\n1. Definition: Work in elementary number theory, formalizable in Peano arithmetic (PA): a prime is an integer greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and itself. The proof uses the PA theorem that every integer greater than 1 has a prime divisor; this is the formal context for the relative-meta-logic contradiction tactic.\\n2. Hypothesis: Assume for contradiction that only finitely many primes exist; call them p₁, p₂, …, pₙ.\\n3. Inference: Form the number N = p₁·p₂·…·pₙ + 1. Then N is an integer greater than 1.\\n4. Inference: By the fundamental theorem of arithmetic, N has a prime divisor q. If q = pᵢ for some i, then pᵢ divides both p₁·p₂·…·pₙ and N, so pᵢ divides their difference, which is 1 — impossible.\\n5. Inference: Hence q is a prime not in the list p₁, …, pₙ, contradicting the assumption that the list was complete.\\nThe assumption fails, so there are infinitely many primes. ∎\\n\\nClarifying questions:\\n1. do you want to weaken the claim into a checkable form (e.g. replace equality with an inequality, or restrict the domain)?\\n2.\"\n+    );\n     assert!(\n         response.answer.contains(\"Disproof\") && response.answer.contains(\"denies a proven theorem\"),\n         \"negated request should be refuted, got: {}\",",

Dropping a credential a job needs fails at release time, on\n/// `main`, in the one workflow no pull request exercises -- so the direction\n/// that matters more is the one that checks that a job which pushes still has\n/// something to push with.\n#[test]\nfn every_checkout_drops_its_credential_unless_it_pushes() {\n    let mut exceptions = Vec::new();\n    let mut swept = 0_usize;\n\n    for path in github_yaml_files() {\n        let name = path\n            .strip_prefix(repository_root())\n            .unwrap_or(&path)\n            .to_string_lossy()\n            .into_owned();\n        let body = fs::read_to_string(&path).expect(\"readable workflow\");\n        let body = body.replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\");\n        let lines: Vec<&str> = body.lines().collect();\n\n        for (index, line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {\n            if !line.contains(\"actions/checkout@\") || line.trim_start().starts_with('#') {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // A `- uses:` line opens the step, so its sibling keys sit one\n            // level deeper; a bare `uses:` is already at that level.\n            let indent = line.len() - line.trim_start().len();\n            let key_indent = if line.trim_start().starts_with(\"- \") {\n                indent + 2\n            } else {\n                indent\n            };\n\n            let mut drops_credential = false;\n            for following in &lines[index + 1..] {\n                if following.trim().is_empty() {\n                    continue;\n                }\n                let following_indent = following.len() - following.trim_start().len();\n                if following_indent < key_indent || following.trim_start().starts_with(\"- \") {\n                    break;\n                }\n                if following.contains(\"persist-credentials: false\") {\n                    drops_credential = true;\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n\n            if drops_credential {\n                swept += 1;\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // An exception has to be argued for where it is written, not in a\n            // list somewhere else that drifts out of date.\n            let reason: String = lines[..index]\n                .iter()\n                .rev()\n                .take_while(|previous| previous.trim_start().starts_with('#'))\n                .map(|previous| previous.trim_start().trim_start_matches('#'))\n                .collect();\n            assert!(\n                reason.contains(\"#1079\") && reason.contains(\"persist-credentials\"),\n                \"{name}:{} keeps its checkout credential without a comment \\\n                 saying why. Set `persist-credentials: [REDACTED]\n                 step in this job pushes with it, write the reason directly \\\n                 above the step and name issue #1079 (issue #1079)\",\n                index + 1\n            );\n            exceptions.push(format!(\"{name}:{}\", index + 1));\n        }\n    }\n\n    assert!(\n        swept >= 44,\n        \"expected the 44 swept checkouts, found {swept}: a checkout that \\\n         stopped being read by this sweep is a checkout that stopped being \\\n         checked\"",

Compare every job's declared `timeout-minutes` against how long that job\n//! actually takes, and fail when the cap has stopped being a backstop.\n//!\n//! ## Why this exists\n//!\n//! Issue #977 established the repository's most expensive class of defect: a\n//! job killed by `timeout-minutes` is reported by GitHub as **cancelled**, not\n//! **failed**. A cancelled job does not turn a run red, does not notify, and\n//! does not appear in the failed-runs view. Eighteen consecutive `main` runs\n//! went untriaged that way.\n//!\n//! Issue #1017 answered it for *steps*: a long step runs under\n//! `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh`, whose budget expires before the job\n//! cap can and exits 124 with an `::error`, so the job reports `failure`. \"The\n//! cap is the backstop; the budget is the deadline.\"\n//!\n//! Nothing answered it for *jobs*. A cap is a constant in a YAML file; the\n//! duration it bounds is only ever observed on GitHub. Issue #1076 measured\n//! 142 `main` runs and found `Coverage / Code Coverage` at **100.7% of its\n//! 40-minute cap** -- it had already crossed, silently, and stayed grey.\n//! `Lint and Format Check` sat at 84.4% and was trending up. Both were caps\n//! that had quietly become deadlines, and nothing in CI could say so, because\n//! nothing in CI had ever looked.\n//!\n//! This script looks. `scripts/collect-job-durations.sh` fetches the\n//! observations from the Actions API; this compares them with what the\n//! workflows declare.\n//!\n//! ## Why a truncated run is still an observation\n//!\n//! The first version of this audit kept only jobs that finished green, on the\n//! reasoning that \"a cancelled or failed job says nothing about how long the\n//! work takes\". Issue #1081 showed that reasoning inverted: the runs a cap or\n//! a budget cuts short are *exactly* the runs at or over the limit, so\n//! discarding them is survivorship bias, and it hides the very thing the audit\n//! looks for. Measured on `Test (macos-15-intel / specification)`, dropping the\n//! two terminated runs reported 62.9% of the cap; keeping them reports 74.7%,\n//! which is the warning band.\n//!\n//! A truncated run is a *lower bound* on how long its work needed. It may\n//! therefore raise a worst case but never lower one, and the report marks it\n//! with a leading `>=` so nobody reads it as a completed measurement.\n//!\n//! ## Why a scheduled audit and not a pull-request gate\n//!\n//! Headroom is a property of a *trend*, not of a commit. A pull request that\n//! changes no workflow can still be the one that pushes a job over, and a pull\n//! request that does change one has no measurements of its own to be judged\n//! against. Committing a measurements file instead would go stale the day it\n//! landed. So the audit re-derives its inputs from the API on a schedule, and\n//! its verdict is about the pipeline as it is running now.\n//!\n//! ## The two bands\n//!\n//! * At or above [`FAIL_SHARE_PERCENT`] the cap is the deadline. Fail.\n//! * At or above [`WARN_SHARE_PERCENT`] the cap is being approached. Warn,\n//!   unless the job is listed in [`ACKNOWLEDGED`] with a reason -- a job whose\n//!   dominant step already owns a budget is bounded by the budget, not by the\n//!   cap, and warning about it every week is the CI noise issue #1076 exists to\n//!   remove.\n//!\n//! A job is judged only once it has [`MIN_SAMPLES`] observations, so a newly\n//! added job is not failed on a single unlucky cold-cache run.\n//!\n//! Usage:\n//!   rust-script scripts/check-job-headroom.rs --durations <file.tsv>\n//!   rust-script --test scripts/check-job-headroom.rs   # inline unit tests\n//!\n//! ```cargo\n143:fn parse_utc_timestamp(value: &str) -> Option<i64> {\n165:fn literal_prefix(name: &str) -> String {\n175:fn declared_jobs(workflow_directory: &Path) -> Vec<DeclaredJob> {\n244:fn measurements(text: &str) -> Vec<Measurement> {\n291:fn match_declared<'a>(\n342:    fn bound_marker(&self) -> &'static str {\n348:    fn share_percent(&self) -> f64 {\n357:fn audit(declared: &[DeclaredJob], measured: &[Measurement]) -> (Vec<Headroom>, Vec<String>) {\n403:fn acknowledgement(job: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {\n411:fn report(rows: &[Headroom], unmatched: &[String]) -> String {\n465:fn main() {\n545:    fn fixture() -> Vec<DeclaredJob> {\n588:    fn measurement(workflow: &str, job: &str, minutes: f64) -> Measurement {\n599:    fn timestamps_parse_as_utc_seconds() {\n610:    fn every_run_that_ran_is_measured_and_the_rest_are_dropped() {\n625:    fn a_step_row_is_not_read_as_a_job() {\n635:    fn a_cut_short_run_raises_the_worst_case_and_is_marked_as_a_lower_bound() {\n659:    fn a_cut_short_run_cannot_lower_the_worst_case() {\n680:    fn the_longest_declared_prefix_wins() {\n691:    fn a_reusable_workflows_job_is_matched_through_its_caller() {\n707:    fn an_expanded_matrix_name_containing_the_separator_is_not_split_on_it() {\n722:    fn a_job_is_not_matched_across_workflows_when_it_is_not_nested() {\n735:    fn the_worst_case_drives_the_share_and_few_samples_are_not_judged() {\n754:    fn frequent_unmatched_names_are_reported_rather_than_dropped() {\n767:    fn workflow_directory() -> std::path::PathBuf {\n776:    fn the_repositorys_own_workflows_parse_into_capped_jobs() {\n806:    fn the_report_names_each_band_and_never_hides_a_row() {\n841:    fn every_acknowledgement_names_a_job_that_exists() {",

This test keeps that list\n// honest: each check exists, runs before merge, and still carries its replay.\n\nimport test from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert/strict';\nimport { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport { join } from 'node:path';\nimport { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';\n\nconst ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../', import.meta.url));\nconst read = relative => readFileSync(join(ROOT, relative), 'utf8');\nconst KINDS = new Set(['js_twin', 'workflow_policy', 'focused_native']);\nconst FIELDS = new Set(['main_run', 'introduced_by', 'failed', 'kind', 'check', 'marker']);\n\n/** The ledger's `regression <id>` blocks; `check` repeats, every other field is single. */\nexport function parseLedger(text) {\n  const entries = [];\n  text.split('\\n').forEach((line, index) => {\n    if (line.trim() === '' || line.startsWith('#')) return;\n    const head = /^regression ([a-z0-9_]+)$/u.exec(line);\n    if (head) {\n      entries.push({ id: head[1], check: [] });\n      return;\n    }\n    const field = /^ {2}([a-z_]+) (.+)$/u.exec(line);\n    if (!field || entries.length === 0 || !FIELDS.has(field[1])) throw new Error(`line ${index + 1}: unreadable ${JSON.stringify(line)}`);\n    const value = field[2].startsWith('\"') ? JSON.parse(field[2]) : field[2];\n    const entry = entries.at(-1);\n    if (field[1] === 'check') entry.check.push(value);\n    else if (field[1] in entry) throw new Error(`line ${index + 1}: ${entry.id} repeats ${field[1]}`);\n    else entry[field[1]] = value;\n  });\n  return entries;\n}\n\nconst ledger = parseLedger(read('data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino'));\nconst inventory = new Set(JSON.parse(read('data/benchmarks/fast-pull-request-javascript-tests.json')).tests);\n\ntest('every recorded regression is complete and unique', () => {\n  assert.ok(ledger.length >= 10, `the ledger keeps the recorded failures (found ${ledger.length})`);\n  assert.equal(new Set(ledger.map(entry => entry.id)).size, ledger.length);\n  for (const entry of ledger) {\n    assert.match(entry.main_run ?? '', /^\\d{11}$/u, `${entry.id}: a GitHub Actions run id`);\n    for (const field of ['introduced_by', 'failed', 'marker']) assert.ok(entry[field], `${entry.id}: ${field}`);\n    assert.ok(KINDS.has(entry.kind), `${entry.id}: kind ${entry.kind}`);\n    assert.ok(entry.check.length > 0, `${entry.id}: at least one pre-merge check`);\n  }\n});\n\ntest('each check exists, runs before merge and still carries the replay', () => {\n  const release = read('.github/workflows/release.yml');\n  for (const entry of ledger) {\n    let replayed = false;\n    for (const check of entry.check) {\n      assert.ok(existsSync(join(ROOT, check)), `${entry.id}: ${check} exists`);\n      if (check.endsWith('.test.mjs')) {\n        assert.ok(inventory.has(check), `${entry.id}: ${check} runs in the fast pull-request inventory`);\n      } else {\n        // The only non-test check is the CI-only PR native check that release.yml calls on pull requests.\n        assert.equal(entry.kind, 'focused_native', `${entry.id}: ${check}`);\n        assert.ok(release.includes(`uses: ./${check}`), `${entry.id}: release.yml calls ${check}`);\n        assert.match(release, /native-type-check:\\n(?: {4}.*\\n)*? {4}if: \\$\\{\\{ !cancelled\\(\\) && \\(github\\.event_name == 'pull_request'/u);\n      }\n      if (read(check).includes(entry.marker)) replayed = true;\n    }\n    assert.ok(replayed, `${entry.id}: one of its checks still carries ${JSON.stringify(entry.marker)}`);\n  }\n});\n\ntest('both main runs of the issue are covered, each by every failure it reported', () => {\n  const byRun = run => ledger.filter(entry => entry.main_run === run).map(entry => entry.id).sort();\n  assert.deepEqual(byRun('43710854562'), ['rust_src_e0308', 'tests_as_docs_loose_only']);\n  assert.deepEqual(byRun('43730270231'), [\n    'clippy_manual_contains', 'gh_read_normalized_payload', 'inline_tests_work_item_leads',\n    'issue_698_planner_expectation', 'module_map_standing_scope', 'top_level_examples',\n  ]);\n});\n\ntest('the parser refuses a field it does not know or a repeated single field', () => {\n  assert.throws(() => parseLedger('regression a\\n  colour \"red\"\\n'), /unreadable/u);\n  assert.throws(() => parseLedger('regression a\\n  kind js_twin\\n  kind js_twin\\n'), /repeats kind/u);\n  assert.deepEqual(parseLedger('# c\\nregression a\\n  check x\\n  check y\\n'), [{ id: 'a', check: ['x', 'y'] }]);\n});\n"

Rust CI/CD starts on every push without waiting for JavaScript checks. The JavaScript gate only parses files. PR #1188 shows the cost: many pushes, almost no green runs. This issue applies the rules from link-assistant/router#759 to this repository.\n35\t\n36\t## Findings\n37\t\n38\t1. **Rust jobs are not gated on JavaScript jobs.** In `.github/workflows/release.yml` the Rust jobs `lint` (line 279), `test` (357, matrix with `cargo test`) and `build` (592) depend only on `detect-changes` and `base`. `coverage.yml` and `layered-ci.yml` also trigger on their own on `pull_request`. No workflow uses `workflow_run`. `layered-ci.yml` orders js, ts and rust tiers only inside itself, and `release.yml` never waits for it.\n39\t2. **The JavaScript gate checks syntax only.** The `js` job in `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml` (lines 89-118) runs `node --check`. The JavaScript tests (`npm run test:web`, `rust/tests/web/*.test.mjs`) run only in `coverage.yml:305` (as coverage) and `links.yml:63`. Both are outside any gate for Rust jobs.\n40\t3. **No JS/Rust behaviour parity gate.** The `ts` tier checks that every `.js` file has a `.ts` sibling (file-set parity). No workflow checks a feature manifest or shared golden fixtures between the JavaScript and Rust implementations. `grep parity .github/workflows` finds only `layered-ci.yml`. CONTRIBUTING.md says the \"closed js-first loop\" is not claimed yet.\n41\t4. **Skipped or cancelled upstream tiers let the next tier run.** `layered-ci.yml` lines 124 and 157 accept `needs.js.result == 'skipped'` and `needs.ts.result == 'skipped'` as pass. A path-filtered or cancelled JavaScript stage therefore does not block the Rust tier.\n42\t5. **Runs are cancelled by the next push.** `release.yml`, `coverage.yml`, `layered-ci.yml` and others set `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, so every PR push cancels the Rust jobs. On #1188 (100 commits, +1,410,501/-200,572): `CI/CD Pipeline` 0/11 green (10 failed, 1 cancelled), `Layered CI` 0/12 (10 failed, 2 cancelled), `Coverage` 0/11 (6 failed, 5 cancelled), `Question necessity ratchet` 5/12 green (7 failed).\n43\t6. **No required status checks on `main`.** The only ruleset, `protection`, has the rules `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`. It has no `required_status_checks` and no pull request rule (`gh api repos/link-assistant/formal-ai/rulesets`).\n44\t7. **No documented single push gate for agents.** CONTRIBUTING.md has \"Work in bulk; verify selectively\" (~line 510) and \"push only after re-reading the issue\" but does not name one agent as the only pusher. It does not say to collect all failures of the latest run before one push, or to never push while a run is in progress. There is no `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` in the repository root.\n45\t8. **Runner OS is not pinned.** `ubuntu-latest` appears 64 times in 28 workflow files. The shared Rust template uses `ubuntu-24.04` and hive-mind `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md` requires an explicit label.\n46\t9. **Daily scheduled workflow is red.** `Self-development status` failed on `main` on 2026-10-05, 06, 07, 08 and 09 (`gh run list --branch main`). `External Benchmarks` also failed on 2026-10-05.\n47\t10. **Stale open pull requests.** #887 (opened 2026-08-01), #652 (2026-07-12), #646 (2026-07-10), #644 and #643 (2026-07-08) are still open.\n48\t11. **No measurement.** No document reports pushes per PR, runs per PR (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, or time to first fully green run for #1188 or a typical PR.\n49\t\n50\t## Requirements\n51\t\n52\t1. Make every Rust job (`lint`, `test`, `build`, coverage, e2e that compile Rust) depend on one JavaScript stage for the same commit. Use `needs:` in one workflow, or `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` and the same `head_sha` and no own `push`/`pull_request` trigger. Test: a PR with a failing JavaScript test starts zero Rust jobs.\n53\t2. Extend the JavaScript stage to run lint, `npm run test:web`, `js/` and `ts/` tests, the js to ts regenerate-and-diff check and the parity check. It must run on every PR, including Rust-only changes.\n54\t3. Add a parity manifest (for example `parity/features.json`, feature to JavaScript implementation, Rust implementation, evidence) with shared golden fixtures that both implementations must pass. Add a checker run in CI. Follow link-foundation/meta-language `parity/language-features.json` and `scripts/check-js-rust-parity.mjs`.\n55\t4. Treat `skipped` and `cancelled` upstream results as failure for the Rust gate. Remove `|| skipped` acceptance in `layered-ci.yml` for the Rust tier, or replace it with an explicit \"unchanged, last green on same tree hash\" check.\n56\t5. Set `cancel-in-progress: false` for the Rust stage on pull request branches, with one concurrency group per branch.\n57\t6. Add a CI check script that fails if any workflow can start a Rust job without the JavaScript gate. Run it in `workflows.yml`.\n58\t7. Add required status checks (the JavaScript stage, the Rust stage and `Pipeline Status`) to the `main` ruleset.\n59\t8. Add the single push gate rules to CONTRIBUTING.md and a new `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`: drafting sub-agents never push; one CI/CD sub-agent pushes once, after collecting all failures of the latest run; never push while a run is in progress on the branch; run JavaScript checks locally before the push; no full local Rust builds unless the change is Rust-only. Include a bounded shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, limited `-j`, and pruning of old artifacts.\n60\t9. Replace `ubuntu-latest` with `ubuntu-24.04` in all workflows and add a check in `scripts/check-ci-workflows`-style form (as in the JS template) that rejects `-latest` labels.\n61\t10. Rust CI/CD starts on every push without waiting for JavaScript checks. The JavaScript gate only parses files. PR #1188 shows the cost: many pushes, almost no green runs. This issue applies the rules from link-assistant/router#759 to this repository.\n\n## Findings\n\n1. **Rust jobs are not gated on JavaScript jobs.** In `.github/workflows/release.yml` the Rust jobs `lint` (line 279), `test` (357, matrix with `cargo test`) and `build` (592) depend only on `detect-changes` and `base`. `coverage.yml` and `layered-ci.yml` also trigger on their own on `pull_request`. No workflow uses `workflow_run`. `layered-ci.yml` orders js, ts and rust tiers only inside itself, and `release.yml` never waits for it.\n2. **The JavaScript gate checks syntax only.** The `js` job in `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml` (lines 89-118) runs `node --check`. The JavaScript tests (`npm run test:web`, `rust/tests/web/*.test.mjs`) run only in `coverage.yml:305` (as coverage) and `links.yml:63`. Both are outside any gate for Rust jobs.\n3. **No JS/Rust behaviour parity gate.** The `ts` tier checks that every `.js` file has a `.ts` sibling (file-set parity). No workflow checks a feature manifest or shared golden fixtures between the JavaScript and Rust implementations. `grep parity .github/workflows` finds only `layered-ci.yml`. CONTRIBUTING.md says the \"closed js-first loop\" is not claimed yet.\n4. **Skipped or cancelled upstream tiers let the next tier run.** `layered-ci.yml` lines 124 and 157 accept `needs.js.result == 'skipped'` and `needs.ts.result == 'skipped'` as pass. A path-filtered or cancelled JavaScript stage therefore does not block the Rust tier.\n5. **Runs are cancelled by the next push.** `release.yml`, `coverage.yml`, `layered-ci.yml` and others set `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, so every PR push cancels the Rust jobs. On #1188 (100 commits, +1,410,501/-200,572): `CI/CD Pipeline` 0/11 green (10 failed, 1 cancelled), `Layered CI` 0/12 (10 failed, 2 cancelled), `Coverage` 0/11 (6 failed, 5 cancelled), `Question necessity ratchet` 5/12 green (7 failed).\n6. **No required status checks on `main`.** The only ruleset, `protection`, has the rules `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`. It has no `required_status_checks` and no pull request rule (`gh api repos/link-assistant/formal-ai/rulesets`).\n7. **No documented single push gate for agents.** CONTRIBUTING.md has \"Work in bulk; verify selectively\" (~line 510) and \"push only after re-reading the issue\" but does not name one agent as the only pusher. It does not say to collect all failures of the latest run before one push, or to never push while a run is in progress. There is no `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` in the repository root.\n8. **Runner OS is not pinned.** `ubuntu-latest` appears 64 times in 28 workflow files. The shared Rust template uses `ubuntu-24.04` and hive-mind `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md` requires an explicit label.\n9. **Daily scheduled workflow is red.** `Self-development status` failed on `main` on 2026-10-05, 06, 07, 08 and 09 (`gh run list --branch main`). `External Benchmarks` also failed on 2026-10-05.\n10. **Stale open pull requests.** #887 (opened 2026-08-01), #652 (2026-07-12), #646 (2026-07-10), #644 and #643 (2026-07-08) are still open.\n11. **No measurement.** No document reports pushes per PR, runs per PR (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, or time to first fully green run for #1188 or a typical PR.\n\n## Requirements\n\n1. Make every Rust job (`lint`, `test`, `build`, coverage, e2e that compile Rust) depend on one JavaScript stage for the same commit. Use `needs:` in one workflow, or `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` and the same `head_sha` and no own `push`/`pull_request` trigger. Test: a PR with a failing JavaScript test starts zero Rust jobs.\n2. Extend the JavaScript stage to run lint, `npm run test:web`, `js/` and `ts/` tests, the js to ts regenerate-and-diff check and the parity check. It must run on every PR, including Rust-only changes.\n3. Add a parity manifest (for example `parity/features.json`, feature to JavaScript implementation, Rust implementation, evidence) with shared golden fixtures that both implementations must pass. Add a checker run in CI. Follow link-foundation/meta-language `parity/language-features.json` and `scripts/check-js-rust-parity.mjs`.\n4. Treat `skipped` and `cancelled` upstream results as failure for the Rust gate. Remove `|| skipped` acceptance in `layered-ci.yml` for the Rust tier, or replace it with an explicit \"unchanged, last green on same tree hash\" check.\n5. Set `cancel-in-progress: false` for the Rust stage on pull request branches, with one concurrency group per branch.\n6. Add a CI check script that fails if any workflow can start a Rust job without the JavaScript gate. Run it in `workflows.yml`.\n7. Add required status checks (the JavaScript stage, the Rust stage and `Pipeline Status`) to the `main` ruleset.\n8. Add the single push gate rules to CONTRIBUTING.md and a new `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`: drafting sub-agents never push; one CI/CD sub-agent pushes once, after collecting all failures of the latest run; never push while a run is in progress on the branch; run JavaScript checks locally before the push; no full local Rust builds unless the change is Rust-only. Include a bounded shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, limited `-j`, and pruning of old artifacts.\n9. Replace `ubuntu-latest` with `ubuntu-24.04` in all workflows and add a check in `scripts/check-ci-workflows`-style form (as in the JS template) that rejects `-latest` labels.\n10. [2026-11-15T17:29:14.756Z] [INFO]           "content": "# Instructions for AI agents working on formal-ai\n\nThis file is for any automated contributor, such as Claude Code, Codex, the\nhive-mind `solve` command or Formal AI itself. `CLAUDE.md` points here.\n[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) still applies in full. This file restates\nonly the rules an agent breaks most often, because each one has cost real CI\ntime ([issue #1191](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1191)).\n\n## The single push gate\n\nA push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the\nprevious run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188\nneeded 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.\nThe rules below make every push count:\n\n1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or\n   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.\n   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.\n2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to\n   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure\n   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same\n   batch.\n3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:\n\n   ```bash\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName\n   ```\n\n   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you\n   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run\n   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).\n4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check\n   apply:\n   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:\n     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;\n   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScript and never compile\n     Rust: `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs --only <gate>`.\n\n   `--list` shows every gate. Run the whole set\n   (`node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs`) before a push that\n   touches shared data such as `data/meta`. The fast pull-request lane runs the\n   same twins, so a failure here would have failed there too.\n5. **No full local Rust build unless the change is Rust-only.** CI compiles\n   Rust: the focused `native-type-check` job on pull requests, and the full\n   matrix on main. Locally, run `rustfmt --check <file>` on the files you\n   changed. That command needs no build.\n6. **If a change is Rust-only and you must build locally, keep the build\n   bounded.** Use one shared target directory for every worktree and agent,\n   with no incremental cache, few jobs, and a prune afterwards:\n\n   ```bash\n   export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=\"$HOME/.cache/formal-ai-target\"  # one directory, shared by all worktrees\n   export CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0                               # no incremental cache to grow without bound\n   export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2                                # a limited -j; scripts/cargo-test.sh also halves CPUs\n   scripts/cargo-test.sh --test unit <filter>               # runs one module, then prunes\n   scripts/prune-build-cache.sh                             # prunes old artifacts after any other cargo command\n   ```\n\n   `scripts/prune-build-cache.sh` follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. It keeps only\n   the latest build's artifacts, and by default it caps the tree at 4 GB\n   locally (`CARGO_TARGET_MAX_SIZE_MB`).\n\n## Where things live\n\n- Production-only failures are recorded in\n  [`data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino`](data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino).\n  These are failures that main recorded after a green pull request. When main\n  fails after a green pull request, add the failure there together with the\n  narrowest pre-merge check that replays it.\n- The fast pull-request JavaScript inventory is\n  [`data/benchmarks/fast-pull-request-javascript-tests.json`](data/benchmarks/fast-pull-request-javascript-tests.json).\n- Runner labels are pinned, and `node scripts/check-runner-labels.mjs` rejects\n  `-latest` labels.\n- Experiments go in `./experiments`. There is no top-level `examples/`\n  directory; Rust examples live in `rust/examples/`.\n- Never commit agent scratch state such as `.claude/`.\n"
