[2026-11-15T17:29:33.052Z] [INFO]           "new_string": "## The single push gate (issue #1191)\n\nEvery push starts the whole pull-request matrix again. A push that fixes only\nsome of the previous run's failures pays that cost once per round trip.\nPull request #1188 needed 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of\nthem was green. Human and AI contributors therefore follow one push gate, which\n[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) restates for agents:\n\n1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** They commit locally or hand back a diff.\n2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** That agent first collects every\n   actionable failure of the latest run on the current head\n   (`gh run list --branch <branch>`, then `gh run view <id> --log-failed`). It\n   fixes all of them in one batch and pushes once.\n3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.**\n   `gh run list --branch <branch> --status in_progress` and `--status queued`\n   must both be empty, unless you are deliberately superseding an older head.\n   The protected-main and superseded-pull-request concurrency groups stay as\n   they are; this rule keeps them from being used as a retry loop.\n4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Run the test files\n   next to the change one at a time\n   (`timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`). Also run the\n   JavaScript twins of the gates the change touches\n   (`node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs --only <gate>`). Run\n   the whole set, without `--only`, before a push that changes shared data.\n5. **No full local Rust build unless the change is Rust-only.** CI compiles\n   Rust: the focused `native-type-check` job on pull requests, and the full\n   matrix on main. `rustfmt --check <file>` needs no build.\n6. **When a Rust-only change has to be built locally, keep the build bounded.**\n   - Share one target directory across worktrees and agents\n     (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$HOME/.cache/formal-ai-target`).\n   - Turn off the incremental cache (`CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`).\n   - Limit the jobs (`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`, or `CARGO_TEST_JOBS=2` for\n     `scripts/cargo-test.sh`).\n   - Prune old artifacts afterwards (`scripts/prune-build-cache.sh`). The\n     script follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` and caps the tree at 4 GB locally.\n\nWhen main fails after a green pull request, record the failure in\n[`data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino`](data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino)\ntogether with the narrowest pre-merge check that now replays it.\n`rust/tests/web/main-only-regression-ledger.test.mjs` keeps each named check in\nthe fast pull-request lane.\n\n## Pull Request Process\n"

This document provides guidelines and instructions for contributing to this project.\n\n**Read [VISION.md](VISION.md) first**, and the architect's notes it is kept up to date from, in [docs/architect-notes/](docs/architect-notes/). It is the standing guideline, in the architect's\nown words: the goal is the meta algorithm; code is held in the meta language and Rust is one emission\ntarget of it; self-modification is an action the user approves; algorithms are arrived at by\ndeduplication; and no task is rated hard -- split it until each leaf is directly solvable. Where any\nother document, gate or requirement contradicts that page, the other one is wrong and must be fixed.\n\n## How we develop Formal AI: drive the Agent CLI, never defer\n\n**Bound retries (issue #1328).** Every retry loop needs a finite attempt ceiling; external IO also needs a finite deadline or cancellation boundary. Count repeated client-owned calls from the transcript, preserving namespace identity and complete failure metadata, even when results are missing or unrecognized. Invalid arguments and local refspec/permission errors require a strategy change or an honest terminal report. Preserve existing safety controls and add a regression that reaches the limit. See [the retry requirement and audit](docs/requirements/issue-1328-bounded-retries.md).\n\n**Method: progressive JPEG (R1188-U28 to R1188-U30).** Every problem and every pull request is attacked the way a progressive JPEG loads: first the whole at low resolution, then sharper passes over all of it, the lowest level first. JavaScript goes first, and the other roots follow by automated translation, with recorded temporary workarounds where the meta language cannot translate yet. See [`docs/progressive-delivery.md`](docs/progressive-delivery.md); [`docs/progressive-plan.md`](docs/progressive-plan.md) is the generated next pass.\n\n**From issue #538 forward, this is the only way we develop the Formal AI\nsystem.** We do not solve a task by editing code and data by hand and we do not\nsolve it partway and defer the rest to a roadmap. We solve it by **driving Formal\nAI through its own [Agent CLI](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent)** (the\nin-repo agentic driver in `rust/src/agentic_coding/`, running against the\nOpenAI-compatible `formal-ai serve` server), and we get *every* requirement done\nin the same pull request.\n\nThis section is the development policy and target workflow, not a claim that\nthe repository is already autonomously self-coded. When an existing tool gap\nforces a manual tool extension, record that boundary plainly, retry a smallest\nleaf through Formal AI, and measure only genuinely session-authored lines. A\nreviewed task decomposition must name its smallest leaves; the acceptance floor\nis at least one real Formal-AI/Agent-CLI-authored leaf out of every five (20%),\nwith a captured session and paired commit trailers. Raise that measured share\nover time; never relabel manual work as self-authored.\n\nConcretely, every change must follow these rules:\n\n1. **The tool authors the change, not you.** Drive the Agent CLI + Formal AI to\n   produce the change. Where the output lands in the repo (e.g. seed data), a\n   test must assert that the committed artifact is **byte-for-byte** what the\n   Agent-CLI-driven recipe produces, so the tool — not a hand-edit — is the\n   author and cannot silently regress. See the issue #538 case study\n   ([`docs/case-studies/issue-538/`](docs/case-studies/issue-538/)) for the\n   pattern and the committed `agent-cli-session*.json` sessions.\n2. **No pre-emptive deferral, no refusals, no follow-ups.** \"This is large or\n   hard\" is never a reason to ship a slice and route the rest to a roadmap. Find\n   the smallest real, tested, reproducible slice of *each* requirement and\n   execute it now, in this PR. Read\n   [`docs/case-studies/issue-538/refusal-anti-pattern.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-538/refusal-anti-pattern.md)\n   before opening a PR — it is the failed reasoning we do not repeat, and we do\n   not teach Formal AI to refuse or defer like that.\n3. **When the tool can't do it, extend the tool, then retry.** Falling back to a\n   manual edit is allowed only after you have proven the Agent CLI / Formal AI\n   cannot yet do it — and then you must immediately improve the Agent CLI /\n   Formal AI so it *can* in general, and re-run through the tool.\n4. **Prove generality with different words each time.** Use a *different* natural\n   language request for each case so a passing run proves the solution is truly\n   general, not hardcoded to one phrasing (issue #538 drives tomato and potato\n   with two differently-worded requests).\n5. **Report faithfully.** State what is done and verified plainly. Honesty means\n   reporting results accurately; it is never a license to stop early or to dress\n   a refusal as an \"honest scope\" section.\n6. **Real Agent-CLI E2E tests in CI, plus a per-requirement test and a\n   whole-task test.** Every change that touches the agentic path must add (or\n   update) a real end-to-end test that boots `formal-ai serve` and drives it\n   with the actual `@link-assistant/agent` CLI over the OpenAI-compatible\n   endpoint — no mocks or in-process shortcuts. Keep the round-trip green in CI\n   (see `test-agent-cli-e2e` in `.github/workflows/release.yml` and the driver\n   script `experiments/agent_cli_e2e/run_agent_cli.sh`). In addition, ship one\n   unit/integration test **per requirement in the issue** and one test that\n   exercises the **whole task** end-to-end so a regression on any single\n   requirement — or on the composition of all of them — breaks the build.\n7. **Hardcoded cases only in tests; production code stays general.** A test may\n   hardcode inputs and expected outputs (that is what a test is *for*), but the\n   engine, planner, seed loader, and Agent-CLI-driven recipes never branch on a\n   specific concept, phrase, or URL. If the only way to make a green case pass\n   is a match-on-literal in `rust/src/`, extend the general routing table (`concept\n   registry`, `capability classifier`, `plan_chat_step`) so future concepts get\n   the same treatment for free.\n8. **Real logs in the case study, not synthesized ones.** When a case study\n   claims the Agent CLI drove the change, it must ship the real captured log of\n   the round-trip (see `docs/case-studies/issue-538/agent-cli-e2e-run.log`), and\n   the committed session JSON must be reproducible byte-for-byte by\n   `cargo test`.\n9. **Commit in small, atomic steps.** Every commit should be independently\n   useful and reviewable — one logical change per commit, buildable in\n   isolation. Interrupted work stays preserved in the PR because each commit\n   already stands on its own; do not batch a day of unrelated edits into one\n   commit.\n\n### Work through the readable source model\n\nFollow [the source-model doctrine](docs/requirements/doctrine-readable-recursive-source-and-comment-meta-language-2026-10-18.md) and [source-model guide](docs/source-representation.md).
