Formalize comment meanings and independently naturalize English documentation; retained text alone is not understanding. Describe parse, emit, synchronization and transformation rules in the meta language, with explicit ambiguity and refusal. Extend the shared meta language where required.\n\nValidate persisted source-free reconstruction, independent reparsing and semantic checks, meaningful held-out edits, exact inverses and cross-language behavior. Remove count-only self-AST fixture maintenance; source content and rules are authoritative. Old signature/histogram tests are historical partial controls and must migrate with their consumers. Prefer the useful invariants researched in meta-language PR #201 and Router PR #761; their numeric serializers and flat token stores are not substitutes for this contract. Keep Rust compilation in CI, source generation bounded, and changes through the authorized Formal AI development loop.\n\n### Verify code, requirements and multilingual documentation together\n\nUse our source and documentation as the core formalization/naturalization corpus. Bind formalized comment/document claims to actual code contracts and evidence, and evaluate them through dependency-aware relative meta logic. Preserve conditional assumptions and shared premises; dependent observations do not become independent support by being counted twice. The same model must support local code/docs and trusted public sources, with explicit unavailable, stale and conflicting evidence.\n\nFormal AI produces English, Russian, Hindi and Chinese documentation through shared meanings. Select wording jointly for measured round-trip meaning survival across every ordered pair, for parts and whole documents; preserve unknown terms, scope, quantifiers, polarity and the original evaluation denominator. CI checks code/doc consistency and formalized requirement delivery. A requirement conflict follows the latest authoritative instruction for that scope, with history retained; a new unrelated instruction does not erase an earlier obligation. Update documentation to match verified requirement-conforming code, and repair code that violates the current requirement. Regenerate and reverify every affected source/document projection after a contradiction-driven edit.\n\n### Testing external agentic CLIs\n\nWhen validating `codex`, `opencode`, `gemini`, or the `agent` CLI against a\nlocal Formal AI server, follow\n[`docs/testing/agentic-cli-tools.md`](docs/testing/agentic-cli-tools.md). The\nguide defines the fixture markers, logging proxy assertions, phrasing matrices,\nand CI shape needed to prove that a result came from Formal AI and that the\nclient actually executed the expected tools.\n\n### Spawn a reference assistant when you need a natural-language target\n\nWhen a change is about *how Formal AI talks* to the user — narration before a\ntool runs, an error explanation, the wording of a question — it helps to see how\na strong conversational assistant would phrase the same step. Spinning up a free\nmodel in `claude`, `codex`, or `opencode` on the *identical* prompt and reading\nits reply gives a concrete, natural target to match, and is a recommended way to\ncalibrate tone before writing the seed catalog text and its tests. Treat those\ntranscripts as reference examples only: the phrasing you ship still lives in the\n`.lino` seed data (never hardcoded in the solver), and every user-visible string\nmust be asserted by a test. Issue #819's narration rewrite was tuned this way —\nthe desirable \"Let me look on your Desktop for …\" shape came from comparing\nFormal AI's output against `claude` and `codex` on the reported request.\n\n### Replaying the self-coding loop\n\n```bash\ncargo build --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --release --bin formal-ai\nrust/examples/self-coding/run.sh\ncargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml self_coding_session_replays\n```\n\nFor a real GitHub issue, run `rust/examples/self-coding/run.sh --live ISSUE_URL`,\nwhich invokes the command below — Hive Mind drives the Agent CLI, which drives\nthe local Formal AI server:\n\n```bash\nsolve ISSUE_URL --tool agent --model formal-ai --attach-logs --verbose\n```\n\n### Formal AI as a subagent on its own requirements (R1026)\n\nKeep what you produce while working on Formal AI in the repository, not in a\nprivate scratchpad, whenever it is worth keeping: probe tools, the gaps found\nby probing, task prompts, claims and sandboxes. Formal AI can then read, edit\nand run it like any other workspace file. The shared folder is\n`experiments/formal_ai_subagent/`, and its `README.md` describes the loop:\n\n1. Delegate a small edit with\n   `node experiments/js_dogfood/drive.mjs --dir <sandbox-or-repo-root> \"<instruction>\"`.\n2. When it fails, probe the cause with `experiments/formal_ai_subagent/probe.mjs`.\n3. Fix the cause generally in both roots, add a regression test, and have\n   Formal AI record the result in the dogfood ledger.\n\nFormal AI keeps its own gap list (`gaps.md`) there too.\n\n### Delegate the next commit to Formal AI: task issue, bot branch, review, merge\n\nThe replay above runs the loop by hand on one machine. The loop we actually\ndevelop by is the same one driven from GitHub Actions, so that no local\nresources are spent and every step leaves reviewable evidence. Each commit we\nwould otherwise write by hand becomes a task Formal AI performs for us, and the\nshare of hand-written commits falls over time.\n\nThe target chain is our own products end to end: **GitHub Actions -> Hive Mind\n-> Agent CLI -> Formal AI**. The action compiles Formal AI from the sources on\nthe branch under review and takes everything else from packages or containers,\nso a run always exercises the meta algorithm as it exists on that branch, spends\nno local resources, and can be adjusted by an ordinary reviewed change to the\nbranch.\n\nToday `.github/workflows/self-authored-pull-request.yml` runs\n**Actions -> Agent CLI -> Formal AI**: it drives the pinned\n`@link-assistant/agent` against a locally built `formal-ai serve` directly,\nbecause `solve --model formal-ai` used to commit none of the trailers or the\nevidence bundle the self-hosting metric attributes\n([hive-mind#2229](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2229)).\nHive Mind fixed that in\n[hive-mind#2230](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2230),\nreleased in v2.24.0; this repository still pins 2.15.1 in\n`.github/workflows/agent-cli-e2e.yml`. Moving the authoring step onto\n`solve … --tool agent --model formal-ai --attach-logs --verbose` behind the\nupdated pin is the remaining step, and it belongs in this loop like any other:\nraise the pin, run one task through it, and compare the commit it produces with\nwhat the direct path produces.\n\nThe steps, in order:\n\n1. **Write the task as an issue.** Small and self-contained: one behaviour, one\n   file where possible. Label it `formal-ai-solve` and give it the contract\n   `.github/workflows/self-authored-pull-request.yml` reads, which is documented\n   in that workflow's header (`task:`, `seed:`, `produces:`, `into:`,\n   `contains:`, `message:`). Make it a sub-issue of the pull request's issue so\n   the delegation is visible from the work it belongs to.\n2. **Let the action author it.** Labelling the issue starts the run. It opens a\n   draft pull request under `github-actions[bot]` first, so the authored commit\n   can name it in its `Formal-AI-Pull-Request` trailer, and it targets the\n   branch the run checked out — the pull request we are working in, not `main`.\n   Then it drives the pinned Agent CLI against a locally built `formal-ai\n   serve` and pushes one commit carrying the four trailers and its evidence\n   bundle. No human commit goes on that branch; a human commit there is the one\n   thing that invalidates the claim.\n3. **Judge the quality on that branch, not in the abstract.** The bot pull\n   request runs the full CI of the repository. Read the diff and the session\n   evidence: did Formal AI make the change asked for, or answer around it? Did\n   it stop after the first clause of a two-part task? Did it route the request\n   somewhere unrelated? The branch is disposable, so this is a cheap experiment.\n4. **If the quality is poor, fix the meta algorithm, not the commit.** Do not\n   hand-correct the bot's work and merge it. Close the branch, record what the\n   session actually did as evidence, file the defect, and improve and generalise\n   Formal AI so the same class of task succeeds — then run the task again. The\n   defects found this way are the point of the exercise, not a detour:\n   [#1095](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1095),\n   [#1096](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1096),\n   [#1099](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1099) and\n   [#1101](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1101) were all\n   found by running tasks this way and reading what came back.\n5. **When satisfied, merge the bot pull request into the working pull request.**\n   Its commits arrive with their trailers intact, so the self-hosting metric\n   attributes them, and the work reaches `main` through the ordinary review of\n   the pull request they merged into.\n\nA draft is finished in one of exactly two ways: **merged**, or **closed with the\ndefect it exposed filed** against the meta algorithm. Leaving it open is\nneither, and it is the failure mode this loop falls into by default — seven bot\npull requests were opened on 2026-09-08 and none was merged. The\n`Self-authored backlog` workflow reports every open one daily with its age, its\ncheck state and how far its base has moved, and fails once one has been open\nmore than three days. Merging the green ones is what turns the loop into\ncommits Formal AI wrote; reading the red ones is what improves it.\n\nTwo rules keep the loop honest. Process record is not authored behaviour: the\nchangelog fragment a source change needs is written by the bootstrap commit that\nopens the bot pull request, because `changelog.d/` is one of the trees the\nmetric excludes from both sides of the share. And the base a run authors against\nmust be current — a bot branch cut before a fix on the working branch fails for\nthat fix's absence, so rerun the task rather than pushing the fix onto the bot\nbranch.\n\n[#1103](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/1103) is the worked\nexample: two commits, both by `github-actions[bot]`, one of them Formal AI's own\nchange to the self-hosting metric with its session evidence beside it.\n\n#### The action is installable in other repositories\n\nThe loop is worth as much to our other repositories as to this one, and it is\nworth most where the volume of new issues is highest. The target is that any\nrepository can install one action and have Formal AI open a draft attempt at\nevery new issue — Hive Mind first, whose issues are the ones we read most often.\nA draft that is wrong is not waste: it fails in public, on a branch nobody\ndepends on, and the failure is the input the next improvement is made from. Fail\nfast to learn fast.\n\nThe loop therefore lives in `.github/actions/author-with-formal-ai`, a composite\naction, and this repository's `self-authored-pull-request.yml` is its first\nconsumer rather than a separate implementation. Three inputs are what make it\ninstallable elsewhere:\n\n- **`formal-ai-source`** — `container` by default, pulling the binary out of\n  `ghcr.io/link-assistant/formal-ai`, so a consuming repository spends no\n  compile. This repository passes `source`, because a change to the meta\n  algorithm has to be measured by the branch making it, not by the last release.\n- **`require-contract`** — `true` demands the `task:`/`seed:`/`produces:`/\n  `into:`/`message:` lines. `false` derives the task from the issue title and\n  body, which is what a repository attempting *every new issue* wants: a draft\n  that fails is the evidence it asked for, not an error.\n- **`formal-ai-ref`** — where the shared scripts come from. They are fetched\n  from this repository rather than vendored into the action, so there is one\n  copy of each to fix; the repository that owns them runs its own branch's\n  copies, so a change to them is testable in the pull request making it.\n\nEvery script the action runs is staged into `RUNNER_TEMP` before anything\nswitches branches. That is not tidiness: run 34224940281 failed on a bug its own\nhead had already fixed, because after `git checkout` of the bot branch the\nscript it ran came off that branch. The CI contract tests read\n`.github/actions/**` as well as `.github/workflows/**` for the same reason — the\nshell CI executes is the same shell whichever directory it sits in.\n\n[hive-mind#2233](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2233) asks\nfor the first outside installation, on `issues: opened`, so every new issue\nthere gets a draft attempt. The drafts it opens are read the same way as here:\njudge the quality on the branch, and when it is poor, improve the meta\nalgorithm.\n\n#### A branch pays for what it changed\n\nUse [the current CI policy](docs/ci-cd/default-branch-builds.md): link parser regressions run by default and full live-link audits remain main-only opt-ins. A historical push to a feature branch\ncost about 310 job-minutes across 16 workflows, and a day of iterating on one\nbranch cost roughly 4,600 — a budget every self-authored draft competes for.\nTwo rules keep that down, and both are measured in\n[#1107](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1107):\n\n- **Build the binary once per source change, not once per workflow.** Seven\n  workflows compiled the same `formal-ai` release binary on every push, two to\n  five minutes each. `.github/actions/formal-ai-binary` keys a cache by the\n  content of `src`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `build.rs`, so a push that\n  changed none of them reuses the build and installs no toolchain at all. Use\n  it from any workflow that only needs to *run* the binary.\n- **Gate the heavy jobs on the files they execute.** `detect-changes` publishes\n  `pipeline-changed` beside `workflow-changed`: the former is true only for the\n  pipeline's own definition, a composite action it calls, or a script those run.\n  The macOS archive, the Docker check, the six box images and the 25-minute\n  agent end-to-end run are gated on it, so editing an unrelated workflow no\n  longer buys them.\n\n- **Do not run a check twice on identical inputs.** `detect-changes` compares\n  the whole pull-request range, so a branch that once touched `rust/src/` used to\n  re-run every Rust check on every later docs-only push. Eight heavy checks\n  now consult `.github/actions/green-ledger`: the content of the check's\n  inputs is hashed (the same key `formal-ai-binary` uses), and a marker saved\n  under that hash by a previous *successful* job means the job announces\n  \"already green\" in its log and step summary and finishes without running\n  its body. The marker rides on `actions/cache`, whose post step runs only on\n  success, so a failing job can never record itself green; `main` never skips.\n  To force a check, edit its workflow file (always part of its inputs) or run\n  it by `workflow_dispatch`. `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1107_green_ledger.rs`\n  pins the contract.\n\nNeither rule may become a silent skip. A job that does not run on a branch is\nreported as not-run, never as passed, and `main` still runs everything.\n\n### Always run automated `solve` sessions with `--attach-logs --verbose`\n\nEvery automated session started against this repository — by hand or by a\nmaintainer's dispatcher — must carry both flags:\n\n```bash\nsolve https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/905 \\\n  --tool agent --model formal-ai --attach-logs --verbose\n```\n\nBoth are load-bearing, and neither substitutes for the other:\n\n- **`--attach-logs`** publishes the session log to the pull request, so a\n  failure leaves behind evidence rather than a single line in a comment.\n- **`--verbose`** is what makes the Agent adapter dump the **raw JSON** of every\n  error record and every fatal startup log record\n  ([link-assistant/hive-mind#2143](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2143)).\n  That raw record is what survives a future payload shape the renderer does not\n  know about.\n\nThis is not a style preference; it is a precondition of the self/auto-learning\nloop this repository is built around. On 2026-08-04 a run on PR #927 failed\nafter 22 seconds and recorded its whole reason as `[object Object]`, with no log\nattached — a failure that is unlearnable by construction, because the next\niteration has nothing to act on. The container is gone and that cause is\nunrecoverable. The full timeline, root causes, and raw evidence are in\n[`docs/case-studies/issue-973/README.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-973/README.md).\n\n`rust/tests/issue_973_solve_flags.rs` enforces the policy: it scans the guides and\nscripts this repository publishes and fails when any `solve` invocation drops\neither flag. Recorded history under `docs/case-studies/`, `dev/log/`, and\n`experiments/` is exempt — a past run stays as it happened.\n\n### Recording self-authorship\n\nThe release metric counts a commit as Formal AI-authored only when its commit\nmessage records the first two trailers below. A contribution intended to\nsatisfy the per-release self-development floor must record all three:\n\n```text\nFormal-AI-Session: <session-id>\nFormal-AI-Evidence: <repo-relative committed evidence path>\nFormal-AI-Pull-Request: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<number>\n```\n\nThe evidence path must exist in that commit. It may name one evidence file or a\ndirectory bundle; one file at or below the path must contain both `formal-ai`\nand the exact session id. Add one pair per session when multiple sessions\nauthored a commit. Do not add these trailers to a human-authored or manually\ncorrected commit. The pull-request reference counts toward the release floor\nonly when Git history proves that the same commit object reached the matching\nGitHub merge commit; a direct commit carrying a claimed PR URL does not count.\nA pull request counts for the work Formal AI did in it, not for what else rode\nalong with it: at least one commit it introduced must carry valid session\nevidence, and every attributed commit it introduced must name that same pull\nrequest. A trailer pointing at a different pull request is not evidence about\nthis one, and it disqualifies the pull request that introduced it. Self-authored\nwork therefore needs no pull request of its own -- it may ride along inside\nordinary review beside human commits, which stay unattributed and stay in the\ndenominator of the metric.\n\nA trailer that turns out to be wrong cannot be corrected in place: this\nrepository's ruleset forbids non-fast-forward pushes on every branch with no\nbypass actors, so a pushed commit message is permanent. A later commit in the\nsame measured range withdraws the claim instead:\n\n```text\nFormal-AI-Retract: <full 40-character sha of the commit being withdrawn>\n```\n\nThe retracted commit stops being attributed, in the pull-request metric and in\nthe release floor alike. The trailer only ever moves a commit *out* of the\nnumerator, so it cannot inflate the measured share; use it to disown a\nmis-trailered commit, never to claim one. It must name a full sha that is\ninside the range being measured, and it may not name the commit carrying it.\n\nThe reviewed prospective policy in `data/meta/self-development-policy.lino`\nsets `presence-mode` to `report` while self-hosting matures. Missing authored\nwork remains visible with its actual counts and `floorSatisfied=false`; it does\nnot block iteration or grant supplied recipes authorship credit. A reviewed diff\nsetting `presence-mode` to `enforce` raises the presence criterion again and\nretains the existing pull-request relaxation after more than 24 hours. Invalid\nclaimed attribution, configuration, Git errors, and independent debt checks still\nfail in either mode. This policy is separate from the numerical share target:\n`target_override_basis_points` on the newest comparable self-hosting ledger row\nis the existing reviewed lever for lowering that target, without changing\nhistorical measurements. The independent strict command\n`rust-script scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs --check-ratchet <base>` requires\nthat the candidate projected trailing share must not decrease relative to\n`<base>` over the same latest-tag release range; a lower candidate returns an\nerror. Presence reporting does not change that numerical comparison. Actual\nrelease recording independently uses Report and records regressions honestly.\nReproduce measured additions plus deletions from non-merge commits, excluding\nbinary files, with\n`rust-script scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs --since <previous-tag>`.\n\nBefore checking the pull-request ratchet locally, fetch annotated release tags\nwith `git fetch origin --tags`; without the latest tag, the check reports a skip.\n\n## Contribution rights and external material\n\nBy intentionally submitting a contribution to this repository, you represent\nthat you have the authority to submit it and offer your copyrightable\ncontribution under the repository's [Unlicense](LICENSE), including its\npublic-domain dedication and permissive fallback terms. If you do not own the\nrights or cannot make that offer, do not submit the material.\n\nThird-party material remains subject to its own license and terms. Identify the\nsource, exact revision, license, required notices, and any naming or use\nconditions in the pull request and repository provenance record. Public access,\nzero price, AI generation, or appearance in an issue does not remove those\nconditions. Follow [LEGAL-COMPLIANCE.md](LEGAL-COMPLIANCE.md) and complete\n[`docs/legal/source-review.md`](docs/legal/source-review.md) before using any\nexternal material for training or distillation.\n\nNever paste or attach any of the following to issues, pull requests,\ndiscussions, logs, fixtures, or commits:\n\n- leaked material or proprietary source code;\n- a paid or access-controlled dataset without redistribution permission;\n- a large verbatim copyrighted work or bulk model output;\n- credentials, private keys, confidential information, or trade secrets; or\n- real personal data.\n\nFor debugging or critique, use the smallest lawful excerpt, link to the\nauthorized source, record provenance, and redact unrelated content. Maintainers\nmay remove, redact, or quarantine suspect material and its downstream copies\nwhile a rights, privacy, safety, or Terms-of-Service concern is investigated.\nRemoval from a public thread is not approval to retain another copy.\n\n## Development Setup\n\n1. **Fork and clone the repository**\n\n   ```bash\n   git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/formal-ai.git\n   cd formal-ai\n   ```\n\n2. **Install Rust**\n\n   Install Rust using rustup (if not already installed):\n\n   ```bash\n   curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh\n   ```\n\n3. **Install development tools**\n\n   ```bash\n   rustup component add rustfmt clippy\n   cargo install rust-script\n   ```\n\n4. **Install pre-commit hooks** (optional but recommended)\n\n   ```bash\n   pip install pre-commit\n   pre-commit install\n   ```\n\n5. **Build the project**\n\n   The repository has three source roots — `rust/` (the crate), `js/` (the\n   hand-iterated web surface) and `ts/` (generated from `js/`); see\n   [docs/source-roots.md](docs/source-roots.md). From the repository root,\n   Cargo commands address the crate through its manifest:\n\n   ```bash\n   cargo build --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml\n   ```\n\n## Development Workflow\n\n1. **Create a feature branch**\n\n   ```bash\n   git checkout -b feature/my-feature\n   ```\n\n2. **Make your changes**\n\n   - Write code following the project's style guidelines\n   - Add tests for any new functionality\n   - Update documentation as needed\n\n3. **Run quality checks**\n\n   ```bash\n   # Format code\n   cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml\n\n   # Lint executable test targets; compile-check examples without linking 100+ binaries\n   cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --lib --bins --tests --all-features\n   cargo check --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --examples --all-features\n\n   # Check file sizes (requires rust-script)\n   rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs\n\n   # Check for hardcoded natural language in rust/src/ (R379, requires rust-script)\n   rust-script scripts/check-hardcoded-language.rs\n\n   # Run all checks together\n   cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --check && cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --lib --bins --tests --all-features && cargo check --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --examples --all-features && rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs && rust-script scripts/check-hardcoded-language.rs\n   ```\n\n4. **Run tests in CI**\n\n   Rust commands below document CI usage. On the workstation, run only one\n   necessary JavaScript test file at a time; never run Rust builds or tests.\n\n   ```bash\n   # Run all tests\n   cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml\n\n   # Run tests with verbose output\n   cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --verbose\n\n   # Run doc tests\n   cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --doc\n\n   # Run a specific test\n   cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml test_name\n\n   # Run the browser unit suite (the site's production JavaScript)\n   npm run test:web\n   ```\n\n   CI job budgets are explicit and workflow-specific; acquisition and setup must leave room for the unchanged test deadline. Rust's built-in `cargo test` runner does not provide a portable global per-test timeout, so wrap long-running network, IO, or async tests with explicit test-level deadlines. If a repository adopts `cargo nextest`, configure runner deadlines with options such as `--slow-timeout` and `--leak-timeout`.\n\n   **Work in bulk; verify selectively.** Draft the whole change set — tests\n   and code together — before running anything, then let it fail in its\n   entirety and fix the failures with as few CI/CD runs as possible.\n   Small-change iteration multiplies CI runs; a batch fixed once is\n   cheaper than ten steps each verified alone. Three rules follow from\n   that:\n\n   - Every plan is drafted in tests and code first. If the drafting is\n     not finished, continue drafting — do not start fixing half a plan.\n   - Run only the specific tests you changed locally (the filter\n     arguments above); rely on CI/CD for everything else. The\n     workstation is a notebook: full suites belong to CI, and\n     sub-agents or helper scripts must never run them locally either.\n   - On long batches, commit at least once every four hours, and push\n     only after re-reading the issue, the pull request, and the diff\n     one more time.\n   - One test at a time on the workstation (R1018): run a single test\n     file (`node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`, after any running\n     `node --test` finishes). When test processes overload the machine,\n     never kill the owner's processes; fix the cause (unbounded\n     concurrency, a runaway runner) instead.\n   - Rust is verified by pushing (R1020): no local `cargo` build, test or\n     clippy. Artifacts that need a Rust build come from CI — the WASM\n     worker from the release workflow's `formal-ai-worker-wasm` artifact,\n     `ts/` from `scripts/translate-es.mjs`.\n   - Keep requirement status current (R1021): a batch that changes what is\n     delivered updates its requirement rows and regenerates the assembled\n     register and the status ledger in the same push.\n   - Never idle-wait on CI (R1022): while a run is in flight, keep drafting\n     the open requirement rows and re-verifying the planned ones. A pull\n     request is finished only when every planned requirement is drafted,\n     CI/CD is green and the release is deliverable.\n   - Decide, don't ask (R1023): open technical choices are settled from the\n     best available practices (researched online when needed), not put to\n     the owner as questions.\n\n   **Use the fast PR / production-main profile (2026-10-28).** Bulk draft related\n   fixes and their tests, requirement updates, vision and guidelines in one PR.\n   Keep essential Linux coding, question-answering and failure-reporting checks\n   on PRs. Retain heavy native, packaging, Docker and integration/E2E jobs rather\n   than deleting them. Production builds, application packaging and Pages deployment\n   run only on main (including its independently authorized release consumers).\n   FORMAL_AI_FULL_PR_CI cannot restore compilation on a PR or branch dispatch.\n   Main still builds and verifies production releases. Full Coding Ladder measurement is main-only opt-in (full-ladder=true or FORMAL_AI_FULL_CODING_LADDER=run); keep its fast consistency gate mandatory and award no deferred measurement credit. Collect complete bounded\n   redacted CI logs, derive small behavioral unit fixtures with negative cases,\n   and fix all available failures before the next push. Never grant execution\n   credit to skipped suites or claim that offline emulation proves a live solve.\n   Real GitHub effects require FORMAL_AI_REAL_GITHUB_E2E=true or explicit dispatch;\n   preserve single-owner custody and trusted outcome-aware cleanup. Run only one\n   necessary JavaScript test locally at a time; no Rust builds or tests locally.\n   Regenerate canonical data mirrors with node scripts/mirror-package-data.mjs\n   --write and commit them; fast lint checks byte equality before merge.\n   Use the ordered runner: Node CLI discovery may sort duration-ranked files alphabetically.\n   Prove execution order with isolated fixtures; retain per-file logs, coverage, concurrency and deadlines.\n   Delivery includes green main CI and verified configured release artifacts.\n   Keep the implementation, regression fixtures, requirements, vision, guidelines\n   and handoff in the same working PR. Verify its exact current head before merge;\n   record the resulting source commit, actual release version and immutable public\n   artifact identities after merge. Earlier releases do not prove this delivery.\n   Reuse the authenticated same-run complete source-history artifact across\n   release consumers; keep the pinned protocol and independent stable-tag and\n   ancestry checks. Explicitly advertise detached source history when negotiating\n   a fetch. Do not retry large redundant downloads or raise their budgets to hide\n   duplication. Missing console evidence after packaging starts remains a failure;\n   record unacquired runners with structured annotations and no execution credit.\n   Exclude private repository source and build outputs from desktop dependencies;\n   verify captured exclusions with the installed packager and audit actual ASAR\n   metadata before installer creation. Preserve required browser/native resources.\n   Refresh governed source witnesses through their reviewed JavaScript generator\n   when referenced files change; run the cheap source-integrity check before push.\n   See [CI speed](docs/ci-cd/speed.md) and the\n   [current requirements](docs/requirements/doctrine-fast-pull-request-production-ci.md).\n\n   **The three-root cycle is js-first.** Rust, JavaScript and TypeScript\n   are all full implementation roots — client and backend — kept\n   equivalent through the meta language rather than by shrinking any\n   root out (standing doctrine of 2026-09-24, R992-R996; it supersedes\n   the 2026-08-04 interfacing-only-JavaScript boundary). Because\n   JavaScript executes faster than Rust compiles, author and test a\n   change in `js/` first when the change touches shared logic, then\n   translate outward rather than hand-porting. The conversion follows\n   the practices of `link-foundation/meta-language` (PR #196) and\n   `link-foundation/relative-meta-logic` (R1024):\n\n   ```bash\n   formal-ai translate --list                  # every direction and its status\n   formal-ai translate --from rust --to meta --input rust/src/module.rs\n   node scripts/self-translate.mjs --to rust js/agentic/crate/module.mjs\n   node scripts/self-translate.mjs --report    # the twins against their Rust\n   node scripts/check-twin-citations.mjs       # every twin cites a live Rust item\n   ```\n\n   `node scripts/self-translate.mjs` is the JavaScript-first self-translation\n   copied from meta-language PR #196: a provenance header, every top-level\n   item translated or carried with the reason\n   `data/meta/self-translation/constructs.lino` gives, and a round trip that\n   restores the source byte for byte (`--to js` reads a translation back,\n   `--to meta` prints the links IR). To widen the fragment, add the construct\n   map row, a case and its `(call ...)` rows to\n   `rust/tests/fixtures/self-translation/cases.lino`, then run\n   `node scripts/self-translate.mjs --write`; never hand-edit the expected\n   files. Both runtimes run every call of that one corpus, the practice of\n   relative-meta-logic's `test-corpus/`. What was adopted and why is\n   [docs/case-studies/pull-request-1188/conversion-best-practices.md](docs/case-studies/pull-request-1188/conversion-best-practices.md).\n\n   Translation in any direction goes through the meta pivot\n   (`rust/src/meta_translate.rs`); a leg that is not materialized yet\n   names the plan-16 leaf that owes it\n   ([plan 16](docs/case-studies/issue-1138/plans/16-js-ts-rust-cycle.md))\n   instead of silently producing nothing. Today only `rust → meta` is\n   live, so the cycle's practical form is still rust-authored; do not\n   claim the closed js-first loop until plan 16 L4 (path-filtered CI)\n   and L5 (CST-equal round trip) land.\n\n   **Delegate to Opus sub-agents only.** Sub-agents are always run on\n   the Opus model; the Fable model must never be used as a sub-agent\n   (project owner directive, 2026-09-15). Keep the agent count low —\n   the workstation is a notebook, and a fleet of agents competes with\n   the build for the same memory: at most two or three sub-agents at\n   once (R1019), each told the same disk, RAM and CPU limits. Sub-agents\n   only make code changes; they run the JavaScript Formal AI only when\n   absolutely necessary and never run builds or full suites.\n\n   **Classify CI failures before touching them.** A branch with\n   tracked, owner-assigned reds (an allowlisted failing test, an\n   evidence gate awaiting a later wave, a rustfmt item already\n   assigned) is not an emergency; fix only failure classes that are\n   new to the branch, and record new standing reds in the owning plan\n   instead of churning the same site twice.\n\n   **Recover requirements from session transcripts.** When auditing\n   that every user directive made it into the requirements, recover\n   the user's messages from the session `.jsonl` transcripts with\n   `experiments/issue_1138_feedback_recovery/collect_user_feedback.py`\n   (it strips harness wrappers, agent reports, and cron echoes) and\n   diff the recovered directives against `docs/requirements/` — new\n   process or architecture notes discovered this way are recorded in\n   this file or the requirements shards, not left in chat history.\n\n5. **Add a changelog fragment**\n\n   For any user-facing changes, create a changelog fragment:\n\n   ```bash\n   # Create a new file in changelog.d/\n   # Format: YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_description.md\n   touch changelog.d/$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)_my_change.md\n   ```\n\n   Edit the file to document your changes:\n\n   ```markdown\n   ### Added\n   - Description of new feature\n\n   ### Fixed\n   - Description of bug fix\n   ```\n\n   **Why fragments?** This prevents merge conflicts in CHANGELOG.md when multiple PRs are open simultaneously.\n\n6. **Commit your changes**\n\n   ```bash\n   git add .\n   git commit -m \"feat: add new feature\"\n   ```\n\n   Pre-commit hooks will automatically run and check your code.\n\n7. **Push and create a Pull Request**\n\n   ```bash\n   git push origin feature/my-feature\n   ```\n\n   Then create a Pull Request on GitHub.\n\n## Code Style Guidelines\n\nThis project uses:\n\n- **rustfmt** for code formatting\n- **Clippy** for linting, with `all`/`pedantic`/`nursery` enabled in `Cargo.toml`'s `[lints.clippy]` (a few noisy lints are explicitly allowed there)\n- **cargo test** for testing\n\n### Code Standards\n\n- Follow Rust idioms and best practices\n- Use documentation comments (`///`) for all public APIs\n- Write tests for all new functionality\n- Keep functions focused and reasonably sized\n- Keep Rust files under 1000 lines (`.lino` files and the browser worker JavaScript are capped at 1500); all limits are enforced by `rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs`\n- Name things in full English words (`index`, not `idx`; `arguments`, not `args`) in code and in the links notation we own, and name files and directories after what they hold, never with numbered parts (R1188-U4, R1188-U5)\n- In the links notation we own, prefer `-` over `_` in names, keep it human readable, and state shared structure once and reference it (R1188-U6, R1188-U7; `docs/links-notation-style.md`)\n- Generalize, don't specialize: fix a failing case with the smallest universal rule that covers its class, so specific tests pass through shared code (R1188-U1), and follow [code-architecture-principles](https://github.com/link-foundation/code-architecture-principles) (R1188-U2)\n- Make bulk changes by rules, such as a substitution pass or a generator with `--check`, not by hand (R1188-U8)\n\n### Documentation Format\n\nUse Rust documentation comments:\n\n```rust\n/// Brief description of the function.\n///\n/// Longer description if needed.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `left` - Description of left\n/// * `right` - Description of right\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// Description of return value\n///\n/// # Errors\n///\n/// Description of when errors are returned\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use my_package::example_function;\n/// let result = example_function(1, 2);\n/// assert_eq!(result, 3);\n/// ```\npub fn example_function(left: i32, right: i32) -> i32 {\n    left + right\n}\n```\n\n## Testing Guidelines\n\n- Run the suite through `scripts/cargo-test.sh` rather than `cargo test`\n  directly. It takes the same arguments and adds two things a workstation\n  needs:\n\n  ```bash\n  scripts/cargo-test.sh                          # whole suite\n  scripts/cargo-test.sh --test unit issue_907    # one module\n  ```\n\n  **Fast local iteration on one test binary.** The test profile ships with\n  `incremental = false` (`Cargo.toml`) — a deliberate CI choice — so every\n  one-line source edit recompiles the whole crate: measured 2m43s for\n  `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --test unit --no-run` after `touch rust/src/lib.rs` on the\n  reference notebook (2 jobs, opt-level 2, `debug = 0` already set). Turning\n  incremental compilation back on locally, in its own target directory so\n  the checked-in profile and the shared cache stay untouched:\n\n  ```bash\n  CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/formal-ai-target-incr \\\n  CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_INCREMENTAL=true CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_INCREMENTAL=true \\\n  CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --offline --test unit -- <filters>\n  ```\n\n  measured **1m11s** for the same touch — a 2.3x faster edit-compile loop —\n  after one 7m05s cold build, with the directory holding ~4.8 GB against\n  ~9.7 GB for the non-incremental one. Keep one directory, not both, when\n  disk is tight, and remember the filters follow `--`\n  (`cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --test unit -- filter_a filter_b`): placed before it, cargo\n  reads them as bin arguments and errors out.\n\n  **macOS runs platform tests, not the whole suite.** No code in `rust/src/` branches\n  on macOS versus Linux — all eight conditionals are `cfg(unix)`, true on both —\n  so pure Rust logic cannot behave differently there. Every macOS-only failure\n  this repository has recorded came from the environment instead: GNU coreutils\n  absent (`timeout`), bash 3.2 without `mapfile`, subprocess and path handling.\n\n  Running everything twice cost real time: 2895 tests moved a 916 MB archive to\n  each of eight runners, 7 GB per run, and two of those downloads failed\n  outright. The macOS lane now runs the 139 tests whose behaviour can differ —\n  about ten seconds on one runner.\n\n  **When something does behave differently on macOS, add its module to\n  `data/meta/macos-platform-tests.lino`** with a line saying what differs. Do\n  not widen the filter back to everything; the file is the list of what macOS is\n  actually for, and `step_budgets_within_job_clocks::the_macos_lane_selects_a_non_empty_set_of_tests`\n  fails if it empties out.\n\n  **Start the longest work first.** Whenever work is split across parallel\n  workers -- test partitions, matrix legs, anything fanned out -- the long tasks\n  must be scheduled first and the short ones packed in behind them. A long task\n  started last runs alone on a machine everything else has already finished\n  waiting for, and that tail is pure serial time on the critical path.\n\n  This is longest-processing-time-first, and it is not a preference: measured on\n  run 32591020809 (2895 tests, 4704s of work over eight partitions), splitting\n  by test index gave a **870s** worst partition against a **588s** ideal, while\n  LPT hit 588s exactly. 282s of the critical path, spent idling.\n\n  `scripts/plan-test-partition.rs` implements it for the macOS test slices from\n  the durations recorded in `data/meta/test-durations.lino`, and the\n  `check-test-partition-balance` CI gate fails when the plan drifts out of\n  balance -- so a regression back to index order cannot land quietly. Apply the\n  same rule to any new fan-out: sort by cost, descending, before assigning.\n\n  **Use the whole machine on CI.** An ephemeral runner is billed for the minutes\n  it is alive, so leaving cores idle only makes the wait longer. Do not add\n  `max-parallel`, and do not cap test threads on CI; the local half-CPU cap\n  below exists for a shared laptop, not for a runner.\n\n  **Half the CPUs locally, all of them on CI.** A bare `cargo test` starts one\n  compile job *and* one test thread per core, which pins the whole machine for\n  the length of the run. The wrapper caps both at half the cores unless `CI` is\n  set, so an ephemeral runner still uses everything it is paying for. Override\n  with `CARGO_TEST_JOBS=<n>`.\n\n  **The cache keeps one build, not every build.** Cargo never removes anything,\n  so `target/` accumulates artifacts from every branch and dependency version\n  and reaches several gigabytes within days. The wrapper prunes to the artifacts\n  the latest build produced, and CI does the same after its test step so the\n  saved actions cache carries one build rather than a growing pile. Run\n  `scripts/prune-build-cache.sh` on its own to reclaim space at any time, or set\n  `CARGO_TEST_NO_PRUNE=1` to keep everything for a debugging session.\n\n  **Every commit sweeps.** The `prune-build-cache` pre-commit hook runs on every\n  commit, not only Rust ones -- a docs-only commit leaves the previous build's\n  artifacts on disk just the same. Disk is reclaimed as a matter of course\n  rather than when someone remembers.\n\n  ```bash\n  cargo install cargo-sweep   # strongly recommended\n  ```\n\n  With cargo-sweep installed the pruner asks cargo *which artifacts the current\n  build actually references* and removes the rest, so a dependency the next\n  build still needs survives even if it was compiled weeks ago. Without it the\n  pruner falls back to comparing modification times, which cannot tell a stale\n  artifact from a current one that simply did not need rebuilding -- it deletes\n  live dependencies and the next build recompiles them. Both keep the cache\n  small; only cargo-sweep keeps it *useful*.\n\n  `CARGO_TARGET_MAX_SIZE_MB` caps the tree after the sweep, defaulting to 4096\n  (4GB) locally and to no ceiling on CI, where the runner is billed for the\n  rebuild rather than the disk.\n\n- Write tests for all new features\n- Maintain or improve test coverage — this is enforced, not requested. CI\n  measures two separate denominators, Rust and browser, against the reviewed\n  floors in `coverage/baseline.json` and fails on a decrease. Raising a floor is\n  a one-liner; lowering one requires an explicit reviewed justification recorded\n  in the file. See [docs/design/coverage-ratchet.md](docs/design/coverage-ratchet.md).\n\n  ```bash\n  # Browser denominator\n  npm run coverage:web && npm run coverage:ratchet -- --only browser\n\n  # Rust denominator\n  cargo llvm-cov --all-features --lcov --output-path lcov.info\n  npm run coverage:ratchet -- --only rust\n\n  # Lock in a gain\n  npm run coverage:ratchet -- --only browser --update-baseline\n  ```\n- Use descriptive test names\n- Organize tests in modules when appropriate\n- Use `#[cfg(test)]` for test-only code\n\nExample test structure:\n\n```rust\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    mod my_feature_tests {\n        use super::*;\n\n        #[test]\n        fn test_basic_functionality() {\n            assert_eq!(my_function(), expected_result);\n        }\n\n        #[test]\n        fn test_edge_case() {\n            assert_eq!(my_function(edge_case_input), expected_result);\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n## Self-maintained dependencies and patches\n\nWhen a build step, the translator, or a layer check needs a feature a\nself-maintained dependency has not released, the workaround is a\n`[patch]`-style source install — and the debt it creates is tracked where\ndebt belongs:\n\n- Every `[patch]` or source-install entry in `Cargo.toml` carries a comment\n  beside it referencing, by URL, the issue that lists what is patched and\n  what blocks using the latest release. The gate\n  `rust/tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_1138_dependency_patches.rs` fails the build when\n  an entry appears without one, and when the lockfile resolves git sources\n  the manifest does not declare.\n- One issue per dependency — not one issue per patch. The issue stays open\n  until the last patch for that dependency is gone.\n- Issues filed against dependencies are written **generally**: state the\n  general case the dependency is missing, not what Formal AI happens to\n  need. The general case moves into the dependency; this repository's own\n  code shrinks. A patch is a bridge, and its issue is the plan to remove\n  it — an untracked patch is invisible debt, because nothing fails when\n  the upstream release lands and nothing ever removes it.\n\nThe same rule governs *held-back releases* (issue #1169): every dependency\nmust sit at its publisher's latest release, and `rust-script\nscripts/check-dependencies-latest.rs` fails when one does not. The one\nsanctioned way to hold a dependency back is a same-line annotation naming\nthe issue that tracks the hold-back — `links-notation = \"0.16.1\" # blocked:\nhttps://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec/issues/60` in\n`Cargo.toml` (the URL may be bare or `<…>`-bracketed), or a `\"<name>//\":\n\"blocked: <url> (reason)\"` note key in the same `package.json`. The\nannotation must open with an issue URL, or with the GitHub security advisory\n(`https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-…`) when the hold-back waits on an\nunpatched vulnerability; a hold-back without one is not a decision, only\ndrift, and the gate fails on it. The daily\n`dependencies-latest` workflow re-checks every registry and opens one pull\nrequest with everything that moved, so the gate being green is a fact about\nyesterday's registries, not a permanent state anyone achieves once.\n\n## GitHub credentials\n\nTokens are **optional in all cases** (issue #1187). Nothing needs\nconfiguring for the workflows to run; when a credential exists, more work\nhappens unattended.\n\n- **One resolver.** Every workflow that writes to GitHub takes its token\n  from `.github/actions/automation-token` — never from a directly read\n  secret. Three layers, first available wins: a GitHub App\n  (`AUTOMATION_APP_ID` + `AUTOMATION_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, one app may serve\n  every repository of the organization), then one secret named\n  `AUTOMATION_TOKEN` — the same name in every repository, so one\n  organization secret serves them all — then the built-in `github.token`.\n  The layer that resolved is printed to the log and the job summary. No\n  other token secret name may appear in a workflow\n  (`rust/tests/unit/issue_1187_credentials.rs` fails the build on one).\n- **Checks without approval.** A `pull_request` workflow run whose PR was\n  opened by `GITHUB_TOKEN` waits for approval — that is GitHub's rule, not\n  ours. When the resolver reports layer `default`, the workflow that\n  pushed the branch calls `.github/actions/dispatch-checks`, which\n  dispatches every `pull_request` workflow on the head commit; dispatch\n  runs need no approval.\n- **Isolation without tokens.** A workload needing a separate tree tests on\n  an orphan branch of this repository (`e2e/<purpose>/<run_id>/<name>`,\n  `.github/workflows/e2e-isolation.yml`), with an `e2e-task` issue and a\n  pull request based on that branch, closed and deleted at the end. A\n  separate repository is used only when the resolver reports\n  `can-create-repositories: true` (the App layer).\n- **Cross-repository work degrades, never fails.** Filing an issue in\n  another repository at layer `default` is not possible; the workload\n  writes its findings into its report (`docs/status.md`, the case study)\n  and keeps one tracking issue here listing what to file.\n\n## Manual confirmation is aspirational (issue #1090)\n\nThe manual-confirmation column of\n[docs/requirements-traceability.md](docs/requirements-traceability.md) is\n**aspirational**: `not yet confirmed` is the honest resting state of a row\nwhose automated test pins the machinery while nobody has yet watched it run\nby hand, and it carries no debt and gates nothing. Two rules follow:\n\n- **No new manual-confirmation ledger may be introduced until an existing one is complete.**\n  A second parallel column would dilute the one surface that exists;\n  finishing beats starting.\n- The way the column fills is the finish branch of #1090: replayed session\n  captures from the agentic-CLI matrix, cited per row. Until a capture\n  exists for a row, the row stays `not yet confirmed` — that is the\n  recorded truth, not a gap to paper over.\n\n## Project Conventions (recurring maintainer recommendations)\n\nThese conventions recur in almost every issue review. They are collected here so\ncontributors — human and AI — can apply them up front instead of rediscovering\nthem in review. They reflect the project's vision: a deterministic, symbolic\nagent whose every answer is a projection of an append-only event log, with no\nhardcoded prompt→answer tables.\n\n1. **Mirror parity (Rust ↔ JS worker).** Every reasoning path in the Rust engine\n   (`rust/src/*.rs`) has a twin in the browser worker (`js/worker/formal_ai_worker.js`\n   loader plus the `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_*.js` shards),\n   so the CLI, library, HTTP server, Telegram bot, and website all answer the\n   same prompt identically. A behavioural change in one **must** be mirrored in\n   the other in the same PR. Name and comment the twin so the parity is obvious\n   (e.g. \"Mirrors `try_x` in `rust/src/solver_handler_x.rs`\").\n   **JavaScript first (REQUIREMENTS.md R997-R1000, 2026-10-06).** Implement\n   and test a requirement in the JavaScript worker first (`npm run test:web`\n   runs in seconds); Rust follows by translation through the meta language,\n   or by a port that names its JavaScript original. Never land a new\n   `null` (\"native surface only\") registry row: `scripts/check-js-parity.mjs`\n   ratchets their count down. A worker module's line ceiling may rise for a\n   JavaScript twin of a native handler, with the keys named in the shard's\n   rationale (R999). Write new handler modules in the portable subset\n   (top-level functions with JSDoc types, `const`/`let`, tagged unions\n   dispatched by `switch`, no classes or destructuring) so they translate\n   mechanically. Regenerate `ts/` with `node scripts/translate-es.mjs\n   --write`; leave Rust compilation to CI — a push is the build.\n\n2. **Data-driven seed, no hardcoded natural language in code (issues #386,\n   #513).** Natural language is *data*, never a string literal in the engine.\n   This applies to **both directions** of every reasoning path:\n   - **Triggers / detection.** All multilingual phrases, surfaces, run verbs,\n     shell tokens, concept summaries, and the tool registry live in\n     `data/seed/*.lino`. Recognisers ask the lexicon for a *meaning* by role\n     (`lexicon().meanings_with_role(ROLE_…)`) or load a named vocabulary\n     (e.g. `seed::terminal_command_vocabulary()`); they never hardcode\n     per-language phrase arrays or branch on literal user phrasings.\n   - **Responses / output.** Every user-facing answer string is a template in\n     `data/seed/multilingual-responses.lino` looked up by intent\n     (`seed::response_for(intent, lang)` in Rust, `answerFor(...)` in the\n     worker). Code fills placeholders like `{command}`; it does not embed the\n     surrounding prose.\n   - **Web front-end (React).** Every string the user sees in `js/app.js`\n     — permission-panel titles, button labels, status words, onboarding copy,\n     system messages — is a catalog entry in `js/i18n-catalog.lino`, looked\n     up at render time via `t(\"<key>\", params)` (the `window.FormalAiI18n`\n     engine). Never pass a prose string literal as a child of `h(...)`; route it\n     through `t(...)` so it follows the active UI language and fills placeholders\n     like `{granted}/{total}`.\n\n   The principle is **meanings ↔ naturalization**: a *meaning* (a slug grounded\n   in seed data) can be *naturalized* into a natural-language surface, and any\n   natural-language word can be *formalized* back into a meaning. Code only ever\n   moves meanings around; the words live in the seed. Add a new cue or answer by\n   editing the `.lino` file and declaring the role/intent — not by typing a\n   phrase into `rust/src/*.rs` or `formal_ai_worker.js`.\n\n   This is enforced by CI, not just convention:\n   - **Total reference-closure gate** (`rust/tests/unit/total_closure.rs` →\n     `scripts/audit-total-closure.py`, run by `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --tests`). Every bare\n     value token in any `data/seed/*.lino` must resolve to a defined meaning, a\n     declared role, a cached dictionary lemma, or a Wikidata id. New vocabulary\n     that resolves to nothing fails the build. Ground new tokens by running\n     `python3 scripts/close-total.py` (idempotent; emits each unresolved token\n     as a first-class meaning under `data/seed/closure-generated-*.lino`) until\n     `python3 scripts/audit-total-closure.py` reports `unresolved_distinct: 0`.\n     Those shards are **content-addressed**: each meaning lands in the shard\n     picked by `sha256(slug) % SHARD_COUNT`, so a new token rewrites exactly one\n     file and leaves the others byte-identical. Do not re-sort them into\n     alphabetical files — filling shards sequentially makes every shard depend\n     on the size of everything before it, which is what made `data/seed`\n     conflict in almost every pull request. `SHARD_COUNT` is fixed rather than\n     derived from the corpus, because changing it reshuffles every shard once;\n     raise it only when a shard approaches the 1500-line data-file limit.\n     `./experiments/issue-909-seed-shard-conflict-blast-radius.sh` asserts the\n     property by adding one token and counting the files it dirties.\n   - **Worker seed parity checks.** Where the JS worker consumes a generated web\n     seed copy, a `--check` guard fails the build on loader regressions and on\n     drift in a present mirror (e.g. the “Check terminal vocabulary worker seed\n     wiring” CI step runs\n     `node experiments/issue-513-sync-worker-terminal.mjs --check`). Refresh\n     the web seed copy with `scripts/sync-seed.sh` or by running the same script\n     without `--check`.\n   - **Web-UI hardcoded-string guard (#511).** `npm --prefix rust/tests/e2e run\n     check:web-hardcoded-ui` parses every `h(...)` call in `js/app.js` and\n     fails the build when a child argument is a bare prose string literal, so new\n     English text cannot leak into the UI. `npm --prefix rust/tests/e2e run check:i18n`\n     asserts every required key exists in all four locales and that sample\n     interpolations render. When you add a web-UI string: add the key + all four\n     translations in `js/i18n-catalog.lino`, register it in `REQUIRED_KEYS`\n     in `rust/tests/e2e/scripts/check-i18n-catalog.mjs`, and render it with `t(...)`.\n\n   See `docs/design/no-hardcoded-natural-language.md` for the full rationale,\n   the meanings ↔ naturalization model, and a worked example.\n\n3. **Roles are declared, then generated.** When you add a meaning with a new\n   `role`, declare it as a `ROLE_*` constant in `rust/src/seed/roles/*.rs`, re-export\n   it from `rust/src/seed.rs`, and regenerate the registry with\n   `python3 scripts/generate-role-registry.py` (keeps `data/seed/roles.lino` in\n   lockstep; enforced by `reference_closure` tests).\n\n4. **Supported-language coverage.** New conversational cues should cover the\n   project's supported languages (currently en, ru, hi, zh). The\n   `rust/tests/e2e/scripts/check-*.mjs` guards fail a one-language change.\n   Translation changes have the stricter issue #526 rule: add or update\n   round-trip tests that prove language-to-meta-to-same-language survival and\n   every supported language-pair path through the meta language. Code\n   translation changes must preserve a `meaning:` link across the source ->\n   target -> source round trip (for example Rust <-> JavaScript), not just render\n   plausible syntax.\n\n5. **Fix everywhere, not just the reported spot.** If a defect has more than one\n   site (most do, because of mirror parity), fix all of them in the one PR.\n\n6. **Reproduce first, then fix.** Add a failing test that reproduces the issue\n   before implementing the fix; a bug fix without a reproducing regression test\n   is treated as incomplete.\n\n   **Benchmark anti-memorization.** A coding-benchmark improvement must come\n   from a reusable task shape, operation meaning, sourced part, or verified\n   composition—not from an upstream case id, entry-point name, or copied task\n   sentence. When the upstream HumanEval/MBPP payloads are cached, run\n   `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --test unit coding_discovery::no_memorization -- --nocapture`;\n   the gate scans `rust/src/` and `data/seed/` against the downloaded slice. A\n   skipped cache is reported explicitly and is not evidence that the gate\n   passed. Generic language/library words need a narrow, reviewed allowlist.\n\n7. **When data is insufficient, add tracing.** If there is not enough signal to\n   find a root cause, add debug output / a verbose mode (default **off**) and\n   keep it in the code so the next iteration has the data.\n\n8. **Case study per issue.** Download the issue's logs and data into\n   `docs/case-studies/issue-{id}/` (raw JSON under `raw-data/`) and write a\n   `README.md` that reconstructs the timeline, enumerates every requirement,\n   finds the root cause(s), surveys prior art / existing libraries, and records\n   the implemented fix and its verification.\n\n9. **Report upstream when relevant.** If an issue is rooted in another\n   repository we can file against, open an issue there with a reproducible\n   example, a workaround, and a suggested fix.\n\n10. **One PR per issue.** Plan and execute everything for an issue in a single\n    pull request; commit atomic, individually useful steps so interrupted work\n    stays preserved.\n\n11. **Prefer the meta algorithm; drive Formal AI to solve its own tasks\n    (direction set by issue #538).** The long-term way we develop this project is\n    to treat every task as a message formalized into the meta language and to let\n    Formal AI — driven through its own Agent CLI\n    (<https://github.com/link-assistant/agent>) — reason about and solve the task\n    by editing its own data (memory) and meta algorithm (reasoning), rather than\n    a human hand-coding each answer. When Formal AI cannot yet perform a step,\n    the goal is to improve the meta algorithm just enough that it can, verifying\n    generality by phrasing the same request different ways and by reproducing the\n    change in a clean repository copy driven by the Agent CLI.\n\n    **Honest current status.** This is not aspirational: from issue #538 forward\n    it is how changes are produced (see the top-of-file rules 1–5). The Agent CLI\n    drives real, byte-for-byte-reproducible changes today — the self-hosting loop\n    (spawn a Formal AI server, hand it the task, capture the Agent-CLI session JSON\n    that reproduces the change) is what wrote the #538 seed data, the potato\n    enrichment, and the generated recipe diagrams; `scripts/reproduce-issue-538.sh`\n    regenerates all three on a clean checkout. What is honestly *not yet built* is\n    autonomous handling of the sweeping, open-ended axes (e.g. a full CST/AST-in-\n    data round trip, or one-shot handling of an arbitrary unseen issue). Those are\n    **not** parked on a roadmap: each names its smallest real, testable next slice\n    in [`docs/case-studies/issue-538/requirements.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-538/requirements.md)\n    and is executed the same way — by extending Formal AI / the Agent CLI until the\n    tool can do it and a test goes red on regression (rule 3), never by hand-editing\n    and deferring. When a task's requirements genuinely conflict (as issue #538's\n    small concrete ask sits inside a much larger vision), surface the contradiction\n    explicitly and still deliver a real, tested slice of *each* axis — never dress\n    \"did part of everything\" as an honest scope cut.\n\n12. **Declare issue disposition explicitly (issue #960; later owner release-iteration requirement R1207-9).** Fully accepted work uses a GitHub [recognised closing keyword](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue), preferably `Fixes https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/146`. An issue whose original acceptance remains unfinished must stay open: use a separate whole line `Related (acceptance pending): https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/146` and state the remaining acceptance. This explicit pending disposition does not claim delivery or close the issue. Ambiguous substitutes such as *Addresses*, *Relates to*, *Part of* and *Refs* still fail `scripts/check-pull-request-link.rs`. Never add a false closing claim just to pass CI.\n\n13. **Case study per pull request.** Alongside the per-issue case study\n    (rule 8), a case study that documents a *pull request* — its review\n    conversation, CI history, and the decisions taken in it — lives in\n    `docs/case-studies/pull-request-{id}/`, mirroring the `issue-{id}` layout\n    (raw JSON under `raw-data/`). Keep issue-driven and PR-driven narratives in\n    their own directories so neither is buried inside the other.\n\n14. **The 1500-line Links Notation cap covers cached data too (issue #960).**\n    `scripts/check-file-size.rs` and `rust/tests/unit/data_files.rs` apply the cap to\n    every `.lino` file in the repository, `data/cache/wikidata/` included.\n    Generated-but-committed is not a reason to be exempt; it is the reason to be\n    measured, because the generator is what can breach the cap. When a fetched\n    response would exceed it, split it into `<bucket>-partN.lino` the way\n    `rust/examples/refresh_translation_cache.rs` already does.\n\n15. **Budget cache buckets: 128 records each (issue #960).**\n    `MAX_SEED_RECORDS_PER_BUCKET` in `rust/src/translation/cache.rs` is enforced, not\n    merely recorded: `scripts/check-cache-budget.rs` fails when a bucket under\n    `data/cache/` holds more than 128 records (a record is a file stem, so\n    `Q1860.json` and `Q1860.lino` count once). Bucket or trim instead of growing\n    past the cap. The three buckets whose size is *forced* by the total-closure\n    gate — `wikidata/entity`, `wordnet/en`, `wiktionary/en`, where every record\n    exists because a seed token references it — are listed as\n    `CLOSURE_DRIVEN_BUCKETS` with a written reason, and pay for the exemption\n    with a stricter invariant: the check fails if any of their records is an\n    orphan nothing references.\n\n16. **Tests are documentation: assert the exact answer (issue #960).** A\n    behavioural or conversational test should show the reader what the system\n    says, not merely that the reply is not empty. Assert the answer verbatim\n    (`assert_eq!(response.answer, \"…\")`, or membership in an explicit list of\n    exact answers) and keep looser `contains` guards only as extra checks\n    *after* the exact one. `scripts/check-tests-as-docs.rs` enforces this as a\n    burn-down ratchet: existing loose-only tests are recorded in\n    `scripts/tests-as-docs-allowlist.txt`, new ones fail the build, and a row\n    that has been made explicit must be pruned (`--write` regenerates the list).\n\n17. **Pin invariants with containment, not byte-equality (R1085-16).** A test\n    that pins a structural invariant — \"this generated document must satisfy\n    property X\" — should assert containment or membership (`assert!(text.contains(…))`,\n    `assert!(VALID_VALUES.contains(&actual))`) rather than comparing the whole\n    generated document byte-for-byte. Byte-equality is right only when the bytes\n    themselves are the contract (a content-addressed artifact, a wire format, a\n    fixture the regeneration pipeline must reproduce exactly). For everything else,\n    pin the observable invariant and leave room for unrelated regeneration to change\n    the surrounding document without breaking the test.\n\n## Merge conflicts are a layout bug (issue #991)\n\n`python3 scripts/analyze-merge-conflicts.py` replays every merge in this\nrepository's history with `git merge-tree` and counts what git could not merge on\nits own. Of 1914 conflict-resolution events across 884 merges, only 37.4% were\ntwo people changing the same behaviour. The rest conflicted because of *where the\ncontent sat*: an appended list entry, a regenerated artifact, a numbered file\nname. Those are bugs in the layout, and the layout is what we fix.\n\nThe measurement is in\n[`docs/case-studies/issue-991/merge-conflict-analysis.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-991/merge-conflict-analysis.md),\nthe mechanisms are declared in\n[`data/meta/merge-conflict-policy.lino`](data/meta/merge-conflict-policy.lino),\nand `rust-script scripts/check-merge-conflict-policy.rs` fails the build when a\npath that has actually been conflicting is neither mechanized nor deferred with\na written reason. **You never need to run `git config` for any of this**: every\nmechanism uses git's built-in `merge=union` driver or a committed generator, so a\nfresh clone is already conflict-proof.\n\n**What to do when you add something.**\n\n| You are adding | Do this | Do *not* |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| a Rust module or test module | append the `mod` line anywhere in the list file; `rust-script scripts/normalize-ordered-lists.rs --write` sorts it | edit the list by hand to keep it sorted — the union driver will reorder it anyway |\n| a CI check | write one file in `data/meta/ci-gates/`, named after the check | add a `- name:`/`- run:` step to `.github/workflows/release.yml` |\n| a `data/seed/*.lino` file | add one `seed <name>` entry to `data/meta/seed-registry.lino` and run `rust-script scripts/generate-seed-registry.rs --write` | edit `rust/src/seed/embedded.rs`, `rust/src/seed/embedded_registry.rs`, `js/seed-files.js`, or the loader's file list |\n| a requirement | write `docs/requirements/issue-NNNN-*.md` and run `rust-script scripts/assemble-requirements.rs --write`; add one row per new ID to `docs/requirements-traceability.md` with the delivery date, the automated test, and an honest `not yet confirmed` while it is not | append a section to `REQUIREMENTS.md` |\n| a worker module | name the file after its subject (`formal_ai_worker_<subject>.js`) | claim the next free number |\n| generated data | commit it and register its regenerate + verify commands in the policy | leave it un-verified: a union merge of an artifact lands silently |\n\n**Documents that are pinned by tests.**\n\nDozens of documentation assertions run in CI, and editing a document without its\npin breaks the build. The mapping, so you know which suite to update:\n\n| Document | Pinned by |\n| --- | --- |\n| `docs/status.md` and the two generated regions in `README.md` and `docs/benchmarks.md` | `rust/tests/unit/documentation_status.rs` — regenerate with `rust-script scripts/render-status.rs --write`; never edit the generated bytes by hand |\n| benchmark statements in `docs/benchmarks.md`, `VISION.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `README.md` | `rust/tests/unit/docs_benchmarks.rs` |\n| `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `docs/requirements/*.md`, `docs/requirements-traceability.md`, and the requirement-status ledger | `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements.rs` and the per-issue modules under `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/` |\n| issue citations across the narrative documents | `rust/tests/unit/documentation_issue_citations.rs` |\n| `docs/architect-notes/` | `rust/tests/unit/architect_notes.rs` |\n| `docs/meta-algorithm.md` and the per-algorithm specification pages | the modules under `rust/tests/unit/specification/` |\n| cross-cutting `README.md`, `VISION.md`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` rules | `rust/tests/issue_885_docs.rs`, `rust/tests/issue_973_solve_flags.rs` |\n| a specific issue's requirement shard | the matching `rust/tests/unit/docs_requirements/issue_NNNN.rs` |\n\n**The two rules behind the table.**\n\n1. **A list belongs in a file of its own.** A list that shares a file with logic\n   cannot be union merged, because a union of two logic edits can compile and\n   still be wrong. Move the list to a sibling file that contains nothing else —\n   `modules.rs`, `worker-modules.js`, `seed-registry.lino` — and union merge only\n   that file. Adding an item then stops being an edit anyone else can collide\n   with.\n2. **Every union-merged file has a verifier.** A union never blocks a merge, so\n   without a checker a stale or duplicated union lands silently. Each\n   union-merged path registers a `verify` command that fails while the unioned\n   result is not canonical, or declares `union_is_terminal true` because every\n   possible union of it is already correct content (only `.gitkeep` qualifies).\n\n**Regenerating everything after a merge.** `bash\nscripts/regenerate-derived-artifacts.sh` runs every registered generator in one\npass; run it after resolving a merge and commit whatever it changes.\n\nIf you hit a conflict that none of this covers, that is data. Add the path to the\npolicy — as a mechanism if it has a shape, or as a `deferred` entry with an\nhonest reason if the collision is genuinely semantic. A deferral with a stated\nreason is a decision; an uncovered path is an omission, and CI treats them\ndifferently.\n\n## Pull Request Process\n\n1. Run only the tests next to your change locally (`node --test <file>`) and\n   the JavaScript twins of the gates it touches\n   (`node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs --only <gate>`); do\n   not build Rust locally. CI runs everything else, and its failures are fixed\n   in bulk (R1188-U24, R1188-U25).\n2. Check the change against the review checklist in\n   [`docs/architecture/principles.md`](docs/architecture/principles.md), which\n   maps every code-architecture principle to the gate that enforces it\n   (R1188-U2), and update documentation if needed\n3. Add a changelog fragment (see step 5 in Development Workflow)\n4. Ensure the PR description clearly describes the changes\n5. Declare each issue's disposition. Address any review feedback\n\n## Changelog Management\n\nThis project uses a fragment-based changelog system similar to [Scriv](https://scriv.readthedocs.io/) (Python) and [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) (JavaScript).\n\n### Creating a Fragment\n\n```bash\n# Create a new fragment with timestamp\ntouch changelog.d/$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)_description.md\n```\n\n### Fragment Categories\n\nUse these categories in your fragments:\n\n- **Added**: New features\n- **Changed**: Changes to existing functionality\n- **Deprecated**: Features that will be removed in future\n- **Removed**: Features that were removed\n- **Fixed**: Bug fixes\n- **Security**: Security-related changes\n\n### During Release\n\nFragments are automatically collected into CHANGELOG.md during the release process. The release workflow:\n\n1. Collects all fragments\n2. Updates CHANGELOG.md with the new version entry; CHANGELOG.md keeps only\n   the newest releases, and older ones roll into `docs/changelog/releases-from-<version>.md`, each named for the oldest release it holds (R1188-U5),\n   so no changelog file exceeds the 1500-line cap\n3. Removes processed fragment files\n4. Bumps the version in Cargo.toml\n5. Creates a git tag and GitHub release\n\n## Project Structure\n\n```\n.\n├── .github/workflows/    # GitHub Actions CI/CD\n├── analysis/             # Ad-hoc analysis notes\n├── changelog.d/          # Dated notes from the architect, indexed in README.md\n├── rust/examples/             # Usage examples\n├── experiments/          # Verification harnesses and one-off experiments\n├── scripts/              # Handler family invoked through the method registry\n│   ├── agentic_coding/   # Agentic-CLI planner, recipes, and driver\n│   ├── proof_engine/     # Decision procedures\n│   ├── summarization/    # Formalize → summarize → deformalize pipeline\n│   ├── translation/      # Docker Compose profiles\n├── CONTRIBUTING.md       # This file\n├── Dockerfile            # Docker-in-Docker Telegram runtime\n├── GOALS.md              # What counts as success\n├── LICENSE               # Issue-by-issue requirement matrix\n├── ROADMAP.md            # Requirement-level implementation status\n└── VISION.md             # Standing guideline and long-term direction; read first\n```\n\n## Release Process\n\nThis project uses semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH):\n\n- **MAJOR**: Breaking changes\n- **MINOR**: New features (backward compatible)\n- **PATCH**: Bug fixes (backward compatible)\n\nReleases are managed through GitHub releases. sorted[middle] : (sorted[middle - 1] + sorted[middle]) / 2;\n};\nconst tally = runs => runs.reduce((counts, run) => {\n  const key = run.status === 'completed' ? run.conclusion : run.status;\n  counts[key] = (counts[key] ?? 0) + 1;\n  return counts;\n}, {total: runs.length});\nconst round = value => value === null ? null : Math.round(value * 10) / 10;\n\nfunction metrics(number) {\n  const [pull] = gh(`repos/${REPO}/pulls/${number}`, '{number, title, created_at, merged_at, closed_at, head: .head.ref, commits, additions, deletions}');\n  const until = pull.merged_at ?? pull.closed_at ?? new Date().toISOString();\n  const runs = gh(`repos/${REPO}/actions/runs?branch=${encodeURIComponent(pull.head)}&per_page=100`,\n    '.workflow_runs[] | {id, name, event, status, conclusion, head_sha, created_at, updated_at}')\n    .filter(run => ['pull_request', 'push'].includes(run.event) && run.created_at >= pull.created_at.slice(0, 10) && run.created_at <= until);\n  const heads = new Map();\n  for (const run of [...runs].sort((a, b) => a.created_at.localeCompare(b.created_at))) {\n    if (!heads.has(run.head_sha)) heads.set(run.head_sha, []);\n    heads.get(run.head_sha).push(run);\n  }\n  const heavy = runs.filter(run => HEAVY.has(run.name));\n  let jobMinutes = 0, listed = 0;\n  for (const run of heavy.slice(0, MAX_JOB_LISTINGS)) {\n    listed++;\n    for (const job of gh(`repos/${REPO}/actions/runs/${run.id}/jobs?per_page=100`, '.jobs[] | {started_at, completed_at, conclusion}')) {\n      if (job.started_at && job.completed_at && job.conclusion !== 'skipped') jobMinutes += Math.max(0, minutes(job.started_at, job.completed_at));\n    }\n  }\n  const firstFailure = [], firstGreen = [];\n  for (const [sha, group] of heads) {\n    const start = group[0].created_at;\n    const failed = group.filter(run => run.conclusion === 'failure').map(run => minutes(start, run.updated_at));\n    if (failed.length) firstFailure.push(Math.min(...failed));\n    const completed = group.every(run => run.status === 'completed');\n    if (completed && group.some(run => run.name === 'CI/CD Pipeline') && group.every(run => GREEN.has(run.conclusion)))\n      firstGreen.push({sha, at: group.reduce((latest, run) => run.updated_at > latest ? run.updated_at : latest, start)});\n  }\n  const green = firstGreen.sort((a, b) => a.at.localeCompare(b.at))[0];\n  return {\n    number: pull.number, title: pull.title, createdAt: pull.created_at, mergedAt: pull.merged_at,\n    commits: pull.commits, additions: pull.additions, deletions: pull.deletions,\n    pushes: heads.size, runs: tally(runs), heavy: tally(heavy),\n    pipeline: tally(runs.filter(run => run.name === 'CI/CD Pipeline')),\n    jobMinutes: Math.round(jobMinutes), jobListings: `${listed}/${heavy.length}`,\n    runsPerPush: round(runs.length / Math.max(1, heads.size)),\n    firstFailureMin: round(median(firstFailure)),\n    firstGreenHours: green ? round(minutes(pull.created_at, green.at) / 60) : null,\n  };\n}\n\nconst numbers = process.argv.slice(2).map(Number).filter(Number.isSafeInteger);\nif (numbers.length === 0) throw new Error('usage: issue-1191-ci-metrics.mjs PR [PR...]');\nconst results = [];\nfor (const number of numbers) {\n  try { results.push(metrics(number)); } catch (error) { results.push({number, error: String(error.message).slice(0, 300)}); }\n  process.stderr.write(`collected #${number}\\n`);\n}\nprocess.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(results, null, 2) + '\\n');\n"

Because release.yml has `paths-ignore` for docs, a required check from it would stay pending forever on docs-only PRs.\n   - **Direct pushes to main.** external-benchmarks.yml pushes its weekly ledger to main via `scripts/push-to-shared-branch.sh`, so any required-checks ruleset needs a bypass actor.\n   - **Ruleset today.** `rules/branches/main` returns only `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`. I am an admin, but chose not to change the ruleset: it is risky and needs human decisions on bypass actors and docs-only PRs.\n   - **Local gates.** `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs` (`--list`, `--only`). shellcheck is at /tmp/w1191/sc/shellcheck-v0.10.0. layered-ci#4 fails only because the environment has no `.meta-language` checkout.\n   - **check-file-size limit:** 1500 lines for maintained text files.\n   - **Ledger and inventory.** The ledger is `data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino`. The fast inventory is `data/benchmarks/fast-pull-request-javascript-tests.json`, keyed `files`, holding entries like \"rust/tests/web/X.test.mjs\".\n   - **GitHub API limits.** The Actions runs listing caps at 1000 results per query. `createEvidenceClient` (scripts/collect-test-replays.mjs) caps responses at 1 MB per request.\n\n3.
