No workflow uses `workflow_run`. `layered-ci.yml` orders js, ts and rust tiers only inside itself, and `release.yml` never waits for it.\\n2. **The JavaScript gate checks syntax only.** The `js` job in `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml` (lines 89-118) runs `node --check`. Both are outside any gate for Rust jobs.\\n3. **No JS/Rust behaviour parity gate.** The `ts` tier checks that every `.js` file has a `.ts` sibling (file-set parity). A path-filtered or cancelled JavaScript stage therefore does not block the Rust tier.\\n5. **Runs are cancelled by the next push.** `release.yml`, `coverage.yml`, `layered-ci.yml` and others set `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, so every PR push cancels the Rust jobs. Add a parity manifest (for example `parity/features.json`, feature to JavaScript implementation, Rust implementation, evidence) with shared golden fixtures that both implementations must pass. Add a checker run in CI. Follow link-foundation/meta-language `parity/language-features.json` and `scripts/check-js-rust-parity.mjs`.\\n4. Remove `|| skipped` acceptance in `layered-ci.yml` for the Rust tier, or replace it with an explicit \\\"unchanged, last green on same tree hash\\\" check.\\n5. Set `cancel-in-progress: false` for the Rust stage on pull request branches, with one concurrency group per branch.\\n6. Add a CI check script that fails if any workflow can start a Rust job without the JavaScript gate. Run it in `workflows.yml`.\\n7. Add required status checks (the JavaScript stage, the Rust stage and `Pipeline Status`) to the `main` ruleset.\\n8. Add the single push gate rules to CONTRIBUTING.md and a new `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`: drafting sub-agents never push; one CI/CD sub-agent pushes once, after collecting all failures of the latest run; never push while a run is in progress on the branch; run JavaScript checks locally before the push; no full local Rust builds unless the change is Rust-only. The historical material records earlier findings; revalidate old claims against current source rather than treating them as new unfixed defects.\n\n\n## Problem\n\nformal-ai is a big Rust project with a JavaScript and TypeScript implementation. Rust CI/CD starts on every push without waiting for JavaScript checks. The JavaScript gate only parses files. PR #1188 shows the cost: many pushes, almost no green runs. This issue applies the rules from link-assistant/router#759 to this repository.\n\n## Findings\n\n1. **Rust jobs are not gated on JavaScript jobs.** In `.github/workflows/release.yml` the Rust jobs `lint` (line 279), `test` (357, matrix with `cargo test`) and `build` (592) depend only on `detect-changes` and `base`. `coverage.yml` and `layered-ci.yml` also trigger on their own on `pull_request`. No workflow uses `workflow_run`. `layered-ci.yml` orders js, ts and rust tiers only inside itself, and `release.yml` never waits for it.\n2. **The JavaScript gate checks syntax only.** The `js` job in `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml` (lines 89-118) runs `node --check`. The JavaScript tests (`npm run test:web`, `rust/tests/web/*.test.mjs`) run only in `coverage.yml:305` (as coverage) and `links.yml:63`. Both are outside any gate for Rust jobs.\n3. **No JS/Rust behaviour parity gate.** The `ts` tier checks that every `.js` file has a `.ts` sibling (file-set parity). No workflow checks a feature manifest or shared golden fixtures between the JavaScript and Rust implementations. `grep parity .github/workflows` finds only `layered-ci.yml`. CONTRIBUTING.md says the \"closed js-first loop\" is not claimed yet.\n4. **Skipped or cancelled upstream tiers let the next tier run.** `layered-ci.yml` lines 124 and 157 accept `needs.js.result == 'skipped'` and `needs.ts.result == 'skipped'` as pass. A path-filtered or cancelled JavaScript stage therefore does not block the Rust tier.\n5. **Runs are cancelled by the next push.** `release.yml`, `coverage.yml`, `layered-ci.yml` and others set `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, so every PR push cancels the Rust jobs. On #1188 (100 commits, +1,410,501/-200,572): `CI/CD Pipeline` 0/11 green (10 failed, 1 cancelled), `Layered CI` 0/12 (10 failed, 2 cancelled), `Coverage` 0/11 (6 failed, 5 cancelled), `Question necessity ratchet` 5/12 green (7 failed).\n6. **No required status checks on `main`.** The only ruleset, `protection`, has the rules `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`. It has no `required_status_checks` and no pull request rule (`gh api repos/link-assistant/formal-ai/rulesets`).\n7. **No documented single push gate for agents.** CONTRIBUTING.md has \"Work in bulk; verify selectively\" (~line 510) and \"push only after re-reading the issue\" but does not name one agent as the only pusher. It does not say to collect all failures of the latest run before one push, or to never push while a run is in progress. There is no `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` in the repository root.\n8. **Runner OS is not pinned.** `ubuntu-latest` appears 64 times in 28 workflow files. The shared Rust template uses `ubuntu-24.04` and hive-mind `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md` requires an explicit label.\n9. **Daily scheduled workflow is red.** `Self-development status` failed on `main` on 2026-10-05, 06, 07, 08 and 09 (`gh run list --branch main`). `External Benchmarks` also failed on 2026-10-05.\n10. **Stale open pull requests.** #887 (opened 2026-08-01), #652 (2026-07-12), #646 (2026-07-10), #644 and #643 (2026-07-08) are still open.\n11. **No measurement.** No document reports pushes per PR, runs per PR (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, or time to first fully green run for #1188 or a typical PR.\n\n## Requirements\n\n1. Make every Rust job (`lint`, `test`, `build`, coverage, e2e that compile Rust) depend on one JavaScript stage for the same commit. Use `needs:` in one workflow, or `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` and the same `head_sha` and no own `push`/`pull_request` trigger. Test: a PR with a failing JavaScript test starts zero Rust jobs.\n2. Extend the JavaScript stage to run lint, `npm run test:web`, `js/` and `ts/` tests, the js to ts regenerate-and-diff check and the parity check. It must run on every PR, including Rust-only changes.\n3. Add a parity manifest (for example `parity/features.json`, feature to JavaScript implementation, Rust implementation, evidence) with shared golden fixtures that both implementations must pass. Add a checker run in CI. Follow link-foundation/meta-language `parity/language-features.json` and `scripts/check-js-rust-parity.mjs`.\n4. Treat `skipped` and `cancelled` upstream results as failure for the Rust gate. Remove `|| skipped` acceptance in `layered-ci.yml` for the Rust tier, or replace it with an explicit \"unchanged, last green on same tree hash\" check.\n5. Set `cancel-in-progress: false` for the Rust stage on pull request branches, with one concurrency group per branch.\n6. Add a CI check script that fails if any workflow can start a Rust job without the JavaScript gate. Run it in `workflows.yml`.\n7. Add required status checks (the JavaScript stage, the Rust stage and `Pipeline Status`) to the `main` ruleset.\n8. Add the single push gate rules to CONTRIBUTING.md and a new `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`: drafting sub-agents never push; one CI/CD sub-agent pushes once, after collecting all failures of the latest run; never push while a run is in progress on the branch; run JavaScript checks locally before the push; no full local Rust builds unless the change is Rust-only. Include a bounded shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, limited `-j`, and pruning of old artifacts.\n9. Replace `ubuntu-latest` with `ubuntu-24.04` in all workflows and add a check in `scripts/check-ci-workflows`-style form (as in the JS template) that rejects `-latest` labels.\n10. Fix or disable `Self-development status` so it is green on `main` for 7 days. Record the root cause in the case study.\n11. This case study with before/after numbers | This document. |\n\n## 4. Root causes\n\n1. **Main-only gates.** Every failure in the ledger has the same shape: a\n   pull request was green, then main failed on a check that pull requests did\n   not run. Rust gates (`check-tests-as-docs.rs`, the module-map test, test\n   placement, the three-source-roots test, the planner tests) ran only on\n   main because they need a Rust build. Fix: a JavaScript twin of each gate in\n   the fast lane, or, where only the compiler can tell (E0308, Clippy), one\n   focused hosted native check.\n2. **Self-development status.** In October the evidence floor reset to 0%\n   after each release tag, so the daily run failed until the floor was\n   recomputed (fixed in 7145aee4e). In November the debt ratchet ran only on\n   main: PR #1495 raised `literal-predicates` to 445 (ceiling 437) and PR\n   #1542 raised `language-parity-gaps` to 52 (ceiling 42). f216155d8 put the\n   ceiling check in the fast lane, and `debt-ceiling-fast-lane.test.mjs`\n   replays both runs.\n3. **Moving runner labels.** `ubuntu-latest` moved to ubuntu-26.04 under an\n   unchanged workflow. That image ships uutils coreutils 0.8.0, whose `mkdir`\n   reports success on `EEXIST` (uutils/coreutils#13970, already reported\n   upstream and closed as fixed; the maintainer pointed to 0.10.0), so two\n   writers both took the `mkdir` lock. Fix: an `O_EXCL` lock and pinned labels.\n4. **Push storms.** #1188 pushed many heads while runs were still going, and\n   each push cancelled the previous runs (finding 5). The fix is a process\n   rule, the single push gate, plus PRs no longer running full Rust at all.\n5. **No ruleset check.** Nothing required a check before merging (finding 6),\n   so a red or pending pipeline did not block a merge.\n\n## 5. Blocked: the maintainer action for requirement 7\n\n`gh api repos/link-assistant/formal-ai/rules/branches/main` returns only\n`deletion` and `non_fast_forward`. Changing the ruleset needs two decisions\nfirst:\n\n- release.yml has `paths-ignore` for docs. GitHub documents that \"if a\n  workflow is skipped due to branch filtering, path filtering, or a commit\n  message, then checks associated with that workflow will remain in a\n  'Pending' state. A pull request that requires those checks to be successful\n  will be blocked from merging\"\n  ([workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/workflow-syntax-for-github-actions)).\n  Docs-only pull requests would then wait forever.\n- external-benchmarks.yml pushes its weekly ledger straight to main\n  (`scripts/push-to-shared-branch.sh`), so the ruleset needs a bypass actor\n  or that push must become a pull request.\n\n`scripts/check-required-status-checks.mjs` runs weekly on main in\n`job-headroom.yml` and fails with the full `gh api -X POST …/rulesets`\ncommand until the ruleset requires `Fast Linux source and requirement\nchecks`, `Native type and lint check / Rust compile inputs changed` and\n`Pipeline Status`. Pull requests run only its fixture test, so they stay\ngreen.\n\n## 6. Before and after\n\nMETRICS_PLACEHOLDER\n\n## 7. Existing components\n\n| Component | Use here |\n| --- | --- |\n| [cargo-sweep](https://github.com/holmgr/cargo-sweep) | Prunes old artifacts from a target directory. `scripts/prune-build-cache.sh` does the same for the repository's layout and now follows a shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. |\n| `scripts/cargo-test.sh` | Limits `-j` and sets `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` for the rare local native run. |\n| link-assistant/router#759, hive-mind `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`, the JS and Rust pipeline templates | The standard the issue applies: pinned labels, one push gate, a JavaScript stage first. |\n| PR #1572 (open) | Fixes the same main-only failures from the CI side. This case study with before/after numbers | This document. |\n\n## 4. Root causes\n\n1. **Main-only gates.** Every failure in the ledger has the same shape: a\n   pull request was green, then main failed on a check that pull requests did\n   not run. Rust gates (`check-tests-as-docs.rs`, the module-map test, test\n   placement, the three-source-roots test, the planner tests) ran only on\n   main because they need a Rust build. Fix: a JavaScript twin of each gate in\n   the fast lane, or, where only the compiler can tell (E0308, Clippy), one\n   focused hosted native check.\n2. **Self-development status.** In October the evidence floor reset to 0%\n   after each release tag, so the daily run failed until the floor was\n   recomputed (fixed in 7145aee4e). In November the debt ratchet ran only on\n   main: PR #1495 raised `literal-predicates` to 445 (ceiling 437) and PR\n   #1542 raised `language-parity-gaps` to 52 (ceiling 42). f216155d8 put the\n   ceiling check in the fast lane, and `debt-ceiling-fast-lane.test.mjs`\n   replays both runs.\n3. **Moving runner labels.** `ubuntu-latest` moved to ubuntu-26.04 under an\n   unchanged workflow. That image ships uutils coreutils 0.8.0, whose `mkdir`\n   reports success on `EEXIST` (uutils/coreutils#13970, already reported\n   upstream and closed as fixed; the maintainer pointed to 0.10.0), so two\n   writers both took the `mkdir` lock. Fix: an `O_EXCL` lock and pinned labels.\n4. **Push storms.** #1188 pushed many heads while runs were still going, and\n   each push cancelled the previous runs (finding 5). The fix is a process\n   rule, the single push gate, plus PRs no longer running full Rust at all.\n5. **No ruleset check.** Nothing required a check before merging (finding 6),\n   so a red or pending pipeline did not block a merge.\n\n## 5. Blocked: the maintainer action for requirement 7\n\n`gh api repos/link-assistant/formal-ai/rules/branches/main` returns only\n`deletion` and `non_fast_forward`. Changing the ruleset needs two decisions\nfirst:\n\n- release.yml has `paths-ignore` for docs. GitHub documents that \"if a\n  workflow is skipped due to branch filtering, path filtering, or a commit\n  message, then checks associated with that workflow will remain in a\n  'Pending' state. A pull request that requires those checks to be successful\n  will be blocked from merging\"\n  ([workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/workflow-syntax-for-github-actions)).\n  Docs-only pull requests would then wait forever.\n- external-benchmarks.yml pushes its weekly ledger straight to main\n  (`scripts/push-to-shared-branch.sh`), so the ruleset needs a bypass actor\n  or that push must become a pull request.\n\n`scripts/check-required-status-checks.mjs` runs weekly on main in\n`job-headroom.yml` and fails with the full `gh api -X POST …/rulesets`\ncommand until the ruleset requires `Fast Linux source and requirement\nchecks`, `Native type and lint check / Rust compile inputs changed` and\n`Pipeline Status`. Pull requests run only its fixture test, so they stay\ngreen.\n\n## 6. Before and after\n\nMETRICS_PLACEHOLDER\n\n## 7. The lock now uses an `O_EXCL` redirection.\n\n**Single push gate** (R8, plan items 4–5)\n- `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are new, and CONTRIBUTING.md gets \"The single push gate (issue #1191)\". GitHub documents that checks of a path-filtered workflow \"will remain in a 'Pending' state\" and block the merge, so docs-only pull requests could never merge.\n2. **The weekly ledger push.** external-benchmarks.yml pushes its weekly ledger straight to main, so it needs a bypass actor.\n\n`scripts/check-required-status-checks.mjs` now runs weekly on main and fails with the exact `gh api -X POST repos/link-assistant/formal-ai/rulesets` command until these checks are required: `Fast Linux source and requirement checks`, `Native type and lint check / Rust compile inputs changed` and `Pipeline Status`. No workflow checks a feature manifest or shared golden fixtures between the JavaScript and Rust implementations. `grep parity .github/workflows` finds only `layered-ci.yml`. A path-filtered or cancelled JavaScript stage therefore does not block the Rust tier.\n5. **Runs are cancelled by the next push.** `release.yml`, `coverage.yml`, `layered-ci.yml` and others set `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, so every PR push cancels the Rust jobs. On #1188 (100 commits, +1,410,501/-200,572): `CI/CD Pipeline` 0/11 green (10 failed, 1 cancelled), `Layered CI` 0/12 (10 failed, 2 cancelled), `Coverage` 0/11 (6 failed, 5 cancelled), `Question necessity ratchet` 5/12 green (7 failed).\n6. **No required status checks on `main`.** The only ruleset, `protection`, has the rules `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`. It does not say to collect all failures of the latest run before one push, or to never push while a run is in progress. There is no `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` in the repository root.\n8. **Runner OS is not pinned.** `ubuntu-latest` appears 64 times in 28 workflow files.
